   207→// computeDiff gets the full branch diff for review. It diffs the current HEAD
   208→// against the merge base with the default branch (main/master), giving the
   209→// reviewer a holistic view of all branch changes rather than just one commit.
   210→func computeDiff(repoRoot string) (string, error) {
   211→	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), wingmanGitTimeout)
   212→	defer cancel()
   213→
   214→	// Find the merge base with the default branch for a holistic branch diff.
   215→	mergeBase := findMergeBase(ctx, repoRoot)
   216→	if mergeBase != "" {
   217→		wingmanLog("using merge-base %s for branch diff", mergeBase)
   218→		diff, err := gitDiff(ctx, repoRoot, mergeBase)
   219→		if err == nil && strings.TrimSpace(diff) != "" {
   220→			return diff, nil
   221→		}
   222→		// Fall through to HEAD diff if merge-base diff fails or is empty
   223→	}
   224→
   225→	// Fallback: diff uncommitted changes against HEAD
   226→	wingmanLog("falling back to HEAD diff")
   227→	diff, err := gitDiff(ctx, repoRoot, "HEAD")
   228→	if err != nil {
   229→		return "", fmt.Errorf("git diff failed: %w", err)
   230→	}
   231→
   232→	// If no uncommitted changes, try the latest commit itself
   233→	if strings.TrimSpace(diff) == "" {
   234→		diff, err = gitDiff(ctx, repoRoot, "HEAD~1", "HEAD")
   235→		if err != nil {
   236→			return "", fmt.Errorf("git diff for latest commit failed: %w", err)
   237→		}
   238→	}
   239→
   240→	return diff, nil
   241→}
   242→
   243→// findMergeBase returns the merge-base commit between HEAD and the default
   244→// branch (tries main, then master). Returns empty string if not found.
   245→func findMergeBase(ctx context.Context, repoRoot string) string {
   246→	for _, branch := range []string{"main", "master"} {
   247→		cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "git", "merge-base", branch, "HEAD") //nolint:gosec // branch is from hardcoded slice
   248→		cmd.Dir = repoRoot
   249→		out, err := cmd.Output()
   250→		if err == nil {
   251→			return strings.TrimSpace(string(out))
   252→		}
   253→	}
   254→	return ""
   255→}
   256→
   257→// gitDiff runs git diff with the given args and returns stdout.
   258→func gitDiff(ctx context.Context, repoRoot string, args ...string) (string, error) {
   259→	fullArgs := append([]string{"diff"}, args...)
   260→	cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "git", fullArgs...) //nolint:gosec // args are from internal logic
   261→	cmd.Dir = repoRoot
   262→	var stdout, stderr bytes.Buffer
   263→	cmd.Stdout = &stdout
   264→	cmd.Stderr = &stderr
   265→	if err := cmd.Run(); err != nil {
   266→		return "", fmt.Errorf("git diff %v: %w (stderr: %s)", args, err, stderr.String())
   267→	}
   268→	return stdout.String(), nil
   269→}
   270→
   271→// resolveWingmanModel returns the model to use for wingman reviews,
   272→// reading from settings with a fallback to the default.
   273→func resolveWingmanModel() string {
   274→	s, err := settings.Load()
   275→	if err != nil {
   276→		return wingmanDefaultReviewModel
   277→	}
   278→	if m := s.WingmanModel(); m != "" {
   279→		return m
   280→	}
   281→	return wingmanDefaultReviewModel
   282→}
   283→
   284→// resolveWingmanAgent returns the agent name to use for wingman reviews,
   285→// reading from settings with a fallback to the default agent.
   286→func resolveWingmanAgent() agent.AgentName {
   287→	s, err := settings.Load()
   288→	if err != nil {
   289→		return agent.DefaultAgentName
   290→	}
   291→	if a := s.WingmanAgent(); a != "" {
   292→		return agent.AgentName(a)
   293→	}
   294→	return agent.DefaultAgentName
   295→}
   296→
   297→// callAgentForReview invokes the configured agent's Prompter to perform a review.
   298→// repoRoot is the repository root so the reviewer can access the full codebase.
   299→func callAgentForReview(repoRoot, prompt, model string) (string, error) {
   300→	agentName := resolveWingmanAgent()
   301→
   302→	ag, err := agent.Get(agentName)
   303→	if err != nil {
   304→		return "", fmt.Errorf("wingman agent %q not found: %w", agentName, err)
   305→	}
   306→
   307→	prompter, ok := ag.(agent.Prompter)
   308→	if !ok {
   309→		return "", fmt.Errorf("agent %q does not support prompting (does not implement agent.Prompter)", agentName)
   310→	}
   311→
   312→	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), wingmanReviewTimeout)
   313→	defer cancel()
   314→
   315→	// Grant read-only tool access so the reviewer can inspect source files
   316→	// beyond just the diff. Permission bypass is safe here since tools are
   317→	// restricted to read-only operations.
   318→	result, err := prompter.Prompt(ctx, prompt, agent.PromptOptions{
   319→		Model:          model,
   320→		WorkDir:        repoRoot,
   321→		AllowedTools:   "Read,Glob,Grep",
   322→		PermissionMode: "bypassPermissions",
   323→	})
   324→	if err != nil {
   325→		return "", fmt.Errorf("agent review prompt failed: %w", err)
   326→	}
   327→
   328→	return result.Text, nil
   329→}
   330→
   331→// readSessionContext reads the context.md file from the session's checkpoint
   332→// metadata directory. Returns empty string if unavailable.
   333→func readSessionContext(repoRoot, sessionID string) string {
   334→	if sessionID == "" {
   335→		return ""
   336→	}
   337→	contextPath := filepath.Join(repoRoot, ".entire", "metadata", sessionID, "context.md")
   338→	data, err := os.ReadFile(contextPath) //nolint:gosec // path constructed from repoRoot + session ID
   339→	if err != nil {
   340→		if !errors.Is(err, os.ErrNotExist) {
   341→			wingmanLog("WARNING: failed to read session context: %v", err)
   342→		}
   343→		return ""
   344→	}
   345→	return string(data)
   346→}
   347→
   348→// staleActiveSessionThreshold is the maximum age of a session state file in an
   349→// ACTIVE phase before it is considered stale (crashed agent) and ignored by
   350→// hasAnyLiveSession. Only applies to ACTIVE/ACTIVE_COMMITTED phases — an IDLE
   351→// session is always considered live regardless of age (user may just be away).
   352→const staleActiveSessionThreshold = 4 * time.Hour
   353→
   354→// hasAnyLiveSession checks if any session is in a non-ENDED phase (IDLE,
   355→// ACTIVE, or ACTIVE_COMMITTED). Used to decide whether to defer review
   356→// application to the prompt-submit injection (visible to user) vs background
   357→// auto-apply (invisible).
   358→//
   359→// ACTIVE/ACTIVE_COMMITTED sessions older than staleActiveSessionThreshold are
   360→// skipped as likely orphaned from crashed processes. IDLE sessions are always
   361→// considered live regardless of age.
   362→func hasAnyLiveSession(repoRoot string) bool {
   363→	sessDir := findSessionStateDir(repoRoot)
   364→	if sessDir == "" {
   365→		return false
   366→	}
   367→
   368→	entries, err := os.ReadDir(sessDir)
   369→	if err != nil {
   370→		return false
   371→	}
   372→
   373→	const maxCheck = 50
   374→	checked := 0
   375→	for _, entry := range entries {
   376→		if checked >= maxCheck {
   377→			wingmanLog("stopping live-session scan after %d entries; assuming live session may exist", checked)
   378→			return true
   379→		}
   380→		name := entry.Name()
   381→		if !strings.HasSuffix(name, ".json") {
   382→			continue
   383→		}
   384→		checked++
   385→
   386→		sid := strings.TrimSuffix(name, ".json")
   387→		info := readSessionPhaseInfo(sessDir, sid)
   388→		if info.Phase == "" || info.Phase == string(session.PhaseEnded) {
   389→			continue
   390→		}
   391→
   392→		// ACTIVE/ACTIVE_COMMITTED sessions that haven't had a real agent
   393→		// interaction in a long time are likely orphaned from crashed agents.
   394→		// Uses LastInteractionTime from JSON (not file modtime) because
   395→		// PostCommit saves all session files on every commit, refreshing
   396→		// modtime even for stale sessions.
   397→		// IDLE sessions are always considered live (user may just be away).
   398→		if session.PhaseFromString(info.Phase).IsActive() {
   399→			if info.LastInteractionTime != nil && time.Since(*info.LastInteractionTime) > staleActiveSessionThreshold {
   400→				wingmanLog("skipping stale active session %s (phase=%s, last_interaction=%s ago)", sid, info.Phase, time.Since(*info.LastInteractionTime).Round(time.Second))
   401→				continue
   402→			}
   403→		}
   404→
   405→		wingmanLog("found live session %s (phase=%s)", sid, info.Phase)
   406→		return true
   407→	}
   408→
   409→	return false
   410→}
   411→
   412→// findSessionStateDir locates the .git/entire-sessions/ directory by
   413→// reading .git to handle both normal repos and worktrees.
   414→func findSessionStateDir(repoRoot string) string {
   415→	gitPath := filepath.Join(repoRoot, ".git")
   416→	info, err := os.Stat(gitPath)
   417→	if err != nil {
   418→		return ""
   419→	}
   420→
   421→	var gitDir string
   422→	if info.IsDir() {
   423→		// Normal repo: .git is a directory
   424→		gitDir = gitPath
   425→	} else {
   426→		// Worktree: .git is a file containing "gitdir: <path>"
   427→		data, readErr := os.ReadFile(gitPath) //nolint:gosec // path from repoRoot
   428→		if readErr != nil {
   429→			return ""
   430→		}
   431→		content := strings.TrimSpace(string(data))
   432→		if !strings.HasPrefix(content, "gitdir: ") {
   433→			return ""
   434→		}
   435→		gitDir = strings.TrimPrefix(content, "gitdir: ")
   436→		if !filepath.IsAbs(gitDir) {
   437→			gitDir = filepath.Join(repoRoot, gitDir)
   438→		}
   439→		// For worktrees, session state is in the common dir
   440→		// .git/worktrees/<name> → ../../ is the common .git dir
   441→		commonDir := filepath.Join(gitDir, "..", "..")
   442→		gitDir = filepath.Clean(commonDir)
   443→	}
   444→
   445→	sessDir := filepath.Join(gitDir, "entire-sessions")
   446→	if _, statErr := os.Stat(sessDir); statErr != nil {
   447→		return ""
   448→	}
   449→	return sessDir
   450→}
   451→
   452→// sessionPhaseInfo holds the subset of session state needed for liveness checks.
   453→type sessionPhaseInfo struct {
   454→	Phase               string
   455→	LastInteractionTime *time.Time
   456→}
   457→
   458→func readSessionPhaseInfo(sessDir, sessionID string) sessionPhaseInfo {
   459→	data, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(sessDir, sessionID+".json")) //nolint:gosec // sessDir is from git internals
   460→	if err != nil {
   461→		return sessionPhaseInfo{}
   462→	}
   463→	var partial struct {
   464→		Phase               string     `json:"phase"`
   465→		LastInteractionTime *time.Time `json:"last_interaction_time,omitempty"`
   466→	}
   467→	if json.Unmarshal(data, &partial) != nil {
   468→		return sessionPhaseInfo{}
   469→	}
   470→	return sessionPhaseInfo{
   471→		Phase:               partial.Phase,
   472→		LastInteractionTime: partial.LastInteractionTime,
   473→	}
   474→}
   475→
   476→// runWingmanApply is the entrypoint for the __apply subcommand, spawned by the
   477→// stop hook when a pending REVIEW.md is detected. It re-checks preconditions
   478→// and triggers claude --continue to apply the review.
   479→func runWingmanApply(repoRoot string) error {
   480→	wingmanLog("apply process started (pid=%d)", os.Getpid())
   481→
   482→	reviewPath := filepath.Join(repoRoot, wingmanReviewFile)
   483→	if !fileExists(reviewPath) {
   484→		wingmanLog("no REVIEW.md found at %s, nothing to apply", reviewPath)
   485→		return nil
   486→	}
   487→	wingmanLog("REVIEW.md found at %s", reviewPath)
   488→
   489→	// Retry prevention: check if apply was already attempted for this review
   490→	state := loadWingmanStateDirect(repoRoot)
   491→	switch {
   492→	case state == nil:
   493→		wingmanLog("no wingman state found, proceeding without session check")
   494→	case state.ApplyAttemptedAt != nil:
   495→		wingmanLog("apply already attempted at %s, skipping", state.ApplyAttemptedAt.Format(time.RFC3339))
   496→		return nil
   497→	default:
   498→		wingmanLog("wingman state loaded: session=%s", state.SessionID)
   499→	}
   500→
   501→	// Re-check session hasn't become active (user may have typed during spawn delay).
   502→	// IDLE and ENDED are safe — only ACTIVE/ACTIVE_COMMITTED should block.
   503→	if state != nil && state.SessionID != "" {
   504→		sessDir := findSessionStateDir(repoRoot)
   505→		if sessDir != "" {
   506→			phaseInfo := readSessionPhaseInfo(sessDir, state.SessionID)
   507→			if phaseInfo.Phase != "" && session.PhaseFromString(phaseInfo.Phase).IsActive() {
   508→				wingmanLog("session is active (phase=%s), aborting (next stop hook will retry)", phaseInfo.Phase)
   509→				return nil
   510→			}
   511→			wingmanLog("session phase=%s, safe to proceed", phaseInfo.Phase)
   512→		}
   513→	}
   514→
   515→	// Mark apply as attempted BEFORE triggering
   516→	if state != nil {
   517→		now := time.Now()
   518→		state.ApplyAttemptedAt = &now
   519→		saveWingmanStateDirect(repoRoot, state)
   520→	}
   521→
   522→	wingmanLog("triggering auto-apply via claude --continue")
   523→	applyStart := time.Now()
   524→	if err := triggerAutoApply(repoRoot); err != nil {
   525→		wingmanLog("ERROR auto-apply failed after %s: %v", time.Since(applyStart).Round(time.Millisecond), err)
   526→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to trigger auto-apply: %w", err)
   527→	}
   528→	wingmanLog("auto-apply completed in %s", time.Since(applyStart).Round(time.Millisecond))
   529→
   530→	return nil
   531→}
   532→
   533→// triggerAutoApply spawns claude --continue to apply the review suggestions.
   534→// NOTE: This uses --continue which is Claude-specific and not part of the
   535→// Prompter interface. If the wingman agent is not claude-code, auto-apply
   536→// is skipped.
   537→func triggerAutoApply(repoRoot string) error {
   538→	agentName := resolveWingmanAgent()
   539→	if agentName != agent.AgentNameClaudeCode {
   540→		wingmanLog("auto-apply skipped: --continue is only supported for claude-code (agent=%s)", agentName)
   541→		return nil
   542→	}
   543→
   544→	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), wingmanApplyTimeout)
   545→	defer cancel()
   546→
   547→	cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "claude",
   548→		"--continue",
   549→		"--print",
   550→		"--setting-sources", "",
   551→		// Auto-accept edits so the agent can modify files and delete REVIEW.md
   552→		// without requiring user consent (this runs in a background process).
   553→		"--permission-mode", "acceptEdits",
   554→		wingmanApplyInstruction,
   555→	)
   556→	cmd.Dir = repoRoot
   557→	// Strip GIT_* env vars to prevent hook interference, and set
   558→	// ENTIRE_WINGMAN_APPLY=1 so git hooks (post-commit) know not to
   559→	// trigger another wingman review (prevents infinite recursion).
   560→	env := agent.StripGitEnv(os.Environ())
   561→	env = append(env, "ENTIRE_WINGMAN_APPLY=1")
   562→	cmd.Env = env
   563→
   564→	var stdout, stderr bytes.Buffer
   565→	cmd.Stdout = &stdout
   566→	cmd.Stderr = &stderr
   567→
   568→	return cmd.Run() //nolint:wrapcheck // caller wraps
   569→}
   570→
   571→// saveWingmanStateDirect writes the wingman state file directly to a known path
   572→// under repoRoot, avoiding os.Chdir (which mutates process-wide state).
   573→func saveWingmanStateDirect(repoRoot string, state *WingmanState) {
   574→	statePath := filepath.Join(repoRoot, wingmanStateFile)
   575→	if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(statePath), 0o750); err != nil {
   576→		return
   577→	}
   578→	data, err := json.MarshalIndent(state, "", "  ")
   579→	if err != nil {
   580→		return
   581→	}
   582→	//nolint:gosec,errcheck // G306: state file is config, not secrets; best-effort write
   583→	_ = os.WriteFile(statePath, data, 0o644)
   584→}

1→// wingman_lifecycle.go contains wingman integration hooks for the lifecycle dispatcher.
     2→// These functions are called from lifecycle.go event handlers to inject wingman
     3→// review state into session start banners, turn start context, and turn end actions.
     4→package cli
     5→
     6→import (
     7→	"context"
     8→	"fmt"
     9→	"log/slog"
    10→	"os"
    11→	"path/filepath"
    12→	"strings"
    13→	"time"
    14→
    15→	"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/logging"
    16→	"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/paths"
    17→	"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/settings"
    18→	"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/strategy"
    19→)
    20→
    21→// wingmanNotificationLockThreshold is the maximum lock file age for showing
    22→// "Reviewing your changes..." notifications. Much tighter than staleLockThreshold
    23→// (used for lock acquisition) because a real review takes at most
    24→// wingmanInitialDelay (10s) + wingmanReviewTimeout (5m) ≈ 6 minutes.
    25→// A lock older than this is almost certainly stale for notification purposes.
    26→const wingmanNotificationLockThreshold = 10 * time.Minute
    27→
    28→// appendWingmanSessionStartStatus appends wingman status to the session start banner.
    29→// Returns the message with wingman status appended.
    30→func appendWingmanSessionStartStatus(message string) string {
    31→	if !settings.IsWingmanEnabled() {
    32→		return message
    33→	}
    34→
    35→	repoRoot, rootErr := paths.RepoRoot()
    36→	if rootErr != nil {
    37→		return message + "\n  Wingman is active: your changes will be automatically reviewed."
    38→	}
    39→
    40→	reviewPath := filepath.Join(repoRoot, wingmanReviewFile)
    41→	if _, statErr := os.Stat(reviewPath); statErr == nil && reviewHasActionableIssues(reviewPath) {
    42→		return message + "\n  Wingman: a review is pending and will be addressed on your next prompt."
    43→	}
    44→	return message + "\n  Wingman is active: your changes will be automatically reviewed."
    45→}
    46→
    47→// handleWingmanTurnStart checks for a pending wingman review and injects it
    48→// as additionalContext so the agent addresses it before the user's request.
    49→// Returns true if a hook response was written to stdout (caller should return early).
    50→func handleWingmanTurnStart(sessionID string) bool {
    51→	if !settings.IsWingmanEnabled() {
    52→		return false
    53→	}
    54→
    55→	repoRoot, rootErr := paths.RepoRoot()
    56→	if rootErr != nil {
    57→		return false
    58→	}
    59→
    60→	wingmanLogCtx := logging.WithComponent(context.Background(), "wingman")
    61→
    62→	// If a review is pending, check if it has actionable issues before injecting
    63→	reviewPath := filepath.Join(repoRoot, wingmanReviewFile)
    64→	if _, statErr := os.Stat(reviewPath); statErr == nil {
    65→		if !reviewHasActionableIssues(reviewPath) {
    66→			// No actionable issues — clean up and notify the user
    67→			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "[wingman] Review has no actionable issues, cleaning up\n")
    68→			logging.Info(wingmanLogCtx, "wingman review has no actionable issues, skipping injection",
    69→				slog.String("session_id", sessionID),
    70→			)
    71→			_ = os.Remove(reviewPath)
    72→			_ = outputHookMessage("[Wingman] Reviewed your changes — no issues found.") //nolint:errcheck // best-effort notification
    73→		} else {
    74→			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "[wingman] Review available: .entire/REVIEW.md — injecting into context\n")
    75→			logging.Info(wingmanLogCtx, "wingman injecting review instruction on prompt-submit",
    76→				slog.String("session_id", sessionID),
    77→			)
    78→			if err := outputHookResponseWithContextAndMessage(
    79→				wingmanApplyInstruction,
    80→				"[Wingman] A code review is pending and will be addressed before your request.",
    81→			); err != nil {
    82→				fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "[wingman] Warning: failed to inject review instruction: %v\n", err)
    83→			} else {
    84→				return true // Hook response written to stdout — caller must return
    85→			}
    86→		}
    87→	}
    88→
    89→	// Notify if a review is currently in progress (fresh lock file).
    90→	lockPath := filepath.Join(repoRoot, wingmanLockFile)
    91→	if lockInfo, statErr := os.Stat(lockPath); statErr == nil && time.Since(lockInfo.ModTime()) <= wingmanNotificationLockThreshold {
    92→		logging.Info(wingmanLogCtx, "wingman review in progress",
    93→			slog.String("session_id", sessionID),
    94→		)
    95→		if err := outputHookMessage("[Wingman] Review in progress..."); err != nil {
    96→			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "[wingman] Warning: failed to output review-in-progress message: %v\n", err)
    97→		}
    98→	}
    99→
   100→	return false
   101→}
   102→
   103→// handleWingmanTurnEnd handles wingman actions at turn end: triggering reviews,
   104→// auto-applying pending reviews, and showing stop notifications.
   105→func handleWingmanTurnEnd(sessionID string, totalChanges int, relModifiedFiles, relNewFiles, relDeletedFiles, allPrompts []string, commitMessage string) {
   106→	repoRoot, err := paths.RepoRoot()
   107→	if err != nil {
   108→		return
   109→	}
   110→
   111→	strat := GetStrategy()
   112→
   113→	// Trigger wingman review for auto-commit strategy (commit already happened
   114→	// in SaveStep). Manual-commit triggers wingman from the git post-commit hook
   115→	// instead, since the user commits manually.
   116→	if totalChanges > 0 && strat.Name() == strategy.StrategyNameAutoCommit && settings.IsWingmanEnabled() {
   117→		triggerWingmanReview(WingmanPayload{
   118→			SessionID:     sessionID,
   119→			RepoRoot:      repoRoot,
   120→			ModifiedFiles: relModifiedFiles,
   121→			NewFiles:      relNewFiles,
   122→			DeletedFiles:  relDeletedFiles,
   123→			Prompts:       allPrompts,
   124→			CommitMessage: commitMessage,
   125→		})
   126→	}
   127→
   128→	// Auto-apply pending wingman review on turn end
   129→	triggerWingmanAutoApplyIfPending(repoRoot)
   130→
   131→	outputWingmanStopNotification(repoRoot)
   132→}
   133→
   134→// triggerWingmanAutoApplyIfPending checks for a pending REVIEW.md and spawns
   135→// the auto-apply subprocess if conditions are met. Called from the stop hook
   136→// on every turn end (both with-changes and no-changes paths).
   137→//
   138→// When a live session exists, this is a no-op: the prompt-submit injection
   139→// will deliver the review visibly in the user's terminal instead. Background
   140→// auto-apply is only used when no sessions are alive (all ended).
   141→func triggerWingmanAutoApplyIfPending(repoRoot string) {
   142→	logCtx := logging.WithComponent(context.Background(), "wingman")
   143→	if !settings.IsWingmanEnabled() {
   144→		logging.Debug(logCtx, "wingman auto-apply skip: wingman not enabled")
   145→		return
   146→	}
   147→	if os.Getenv("ENTIRE_WINGMAN_APPLY") != "" {
   148→		logging.Debug(logCtx, "wingman auto-apply skip: already in apply subprocess")
   149→		return
   150→	}
   151→	reviewPath := filepath.Join(repoRoot, wingmanReviewFile)
   152→	if _, statErr := os.Stat(reviewPath); statErr != nil {
   153→		logging.Debug(logCtx, "wingman auto-apply skip: no REVIEW.md pending")
   154→		return
   155→	}
   156→	// Skip auto-apply if the review has no actionable issues
   157→	if !reviewHasActionableIssues(reviewPath) {
   158→		logging.Info(logCtx, "wingman auto-apply skip: review has no actionable issues, cleaning up")
   159→		_ = os.Remove(reviewPath)
   160→		return
   161→	}
   162→	wingmanState := loadWingmanStateDirect(repoRoot)
   163→	if wingmanState != nil && wingmanState.ApplyAttemptedAt != nil {
   164→		logging.Debug(logCtx, "wingman auto-apply already attempted, skipping",
   165→			slog.Time("attempted_at", *wingmanState.ApplyAttemptedAt),
   166→		)
   167→		return
   168→	}
   169→	// Don't spawn background auto-apply if a live session exists.
   170→	// The prompt-submit hook will inject REVIEW.md as additionalContext,
   171→	// which is visible to the user in their terminal.
   172→	if hasAnyLiveSession(repoRoot) {
   173→		logging.Debug(logCtx, "wingman auto-apply deferred: live session will handle via injection")
   174→		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "[wingman] Review pending — will be injected on next prompt\n")
   175→		return
   176→	}
   177→	fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "[wingman] Pending review found, spawning auto-apply (no live sessions)\n")
   178→	logging.Info(logCtx, "wingman auto-apply spawning (no live sessions)",
   179→		slog.String("review_path", reviewPath),
   180→	)
   181→	spawnDetachedWingmanApply(repoRoot)
   182→}
   183→
   184→// reviewHasActionableIssues reads a REVIEW.md and checks if it contains
   185→// actionable issue markers ([CRITICAL], [WARNING], or [SUGGESTION]).
   186→// Returns false if the file can't be read or contains no issues.
   187→func reviewHasActionableIssues(reviewPath string) bool {
   188→	data, err := os.ReadFile(reviewPath) //nolint:gosec // path is from repo-relative constant
   189→	if err != nil {
   190→		return false
   191→	}
   192→
   193→	content := string(data)
   194→
   195→	// The review format uses "### [SEVERITY] description" for each issue.
   196→	// Check for any of the severity markers in heading context.
   197→	for _, marker := range []string{"[CRITICAL]", "[WARNING]", "[SUGGESTION]"} {
   198→		if strings.Contains(content, marker) {

    18→## Session Context
    19→
    20→This review is part of an automated development workflow. The developer works with an AI coding agent that makes changes on their behalf. Below is the checkpoint data captured during the session, which tells you WHY these changes were made.

    61→**Correctness**:

1→package agent
     2→
     3→import (
     4→	"fmt"
     5→	"slices"
     6→	"sync"
     7→)
     8→
     9→var (
    10→	registryMu sync.RWMutex
    11→	registry   = make(map[AgentName]Factory)
    12→)
    13→
    14→// Factory creates a new agent instance
    15→type Factory func() Agent
    16→
    17→// Register adds an agent factory to the registry.
    18→// Called from init() in each agent implementation.
    19→func Register(name AgentName, factory Factory) {
    20→	registryMu.Lock()
    21→	defer registryMu.Unlock()
    22→	registry[name] = factory
    23→}
    24→
    25→// Get retrieves an agent by name.
    26→//
    27→
    28→func Get(name AgentName) (Agent, error) {
    29→	registryMu.RLock()
    30→	defer registryMu.RUnlock()
    31→
    32→	factory, ok := registry[name]
    33→	if !ok {
    34→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("unknown agent: %s (available: %v)", name, List())
    35→	}
    36→	return factory(), nil
    37→}
    38→
    39→// List returns all registered agent names in sorted order.
    40→func List() []AgentName {
    41→	registryMu.RLock()
    42→	defer registryMu.RUnlock()
    43→
    44→	names := make([]AgentName, 0, len(registry))
    45→	for name := range registry {
    46→		names = append(names, name)
    47→	}
    48→	slices.Sort(names)
    49→	return names
    50→}
    51→
    52→// DetectAll returns all agents whose DetectPresence reports true.
    53→// Agents are checked in sorted name order (via List()) for deterministic results.
    54→// Returns an empty slice when no agent is detected.
    55→func DetectAll() []Agent {
    56→	names := List() // sorted, lock-safe
    57→
    58→	var detected []Agent
    59→	for _, name := range names {
    60→		ag, err := Get(name)
    61→		if err != nil {
    62→			continue
    63→		}
    64→		if present, err := ag.DetectPresence(); err == nil && present {
    65→			detected = append(detected, ag)
    66→		}
    67→	}
    68→	return detected
    69→}
    70→
    71→// Detect attempts to auto-detect which agent is being used.
    72→// Iterates registered agents in sorted name order for deterministic results.
    73→// Returns the first agent whose DetectPresence reports true.
    74→func Detect() (Agent, error) {
    75→	detected := DetectAll()
    76→	if len(detected) == 0 {
    77→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("no agent detected (available: %v)", List())
    78→	}
    79→	return detected[0], nil
    80→}
    81→
    82→// AgentName is the registry key type for agents (e.g., "claude-code", "gemini").
    83→//
    84→//nolint:revive // stuttering is intentional - distinguishes from AgentType when both are used
    85→type AgentName string
    86→
    87→// AgentType is the display name type stored in metadata/trailers (e.g., "Claude Code", "Gemini CLI").
    88→//
    89→//nolint:revive // stuttering is intentional - distinguishes from AgentName when both are used
    90→type AgentType string
    91→
    92→// Agent name constants (registry keys)
    93→const (
    94→	AgentNameClaudeCode AgentName = "claude-code"
    95→	AgentNameGemini     AgentName = "gemini"
    96→)
    97→
    98→// Agent type constants (type identifiers stored in metadata/trailers)
    99→const (

## Wingman CLI Command Structure and Configuration

Based on my thorough exploration of the codebase, here's the complete wingman command architecture:

### 1. **Command Definitions** (`/Users/dip/Repositories/cli/cmd/entire/cli/wingman.go`)

**Main Command: `entire wingman`**
- Short: "Automated code review for agent sessions"
- Subcommands:
  - `enable` - Enable wingman auto-review
  - `disable` - Disable wingman auto-review
  - `status` - Show wingman status

**Wingman Enable Command** (`newWingmanEnableCmd`)

**Wingman Disable Command** (`newWingmanDisableCmd`)
- Flags:
  - `--local` (bool, default: false) - Write to settings.local.json instead of settings.json

**Wingman Status Command** (`newWingmanStatusCmd`)
- No flags

**Wingman Apply Command** (`newWingmanApplyCmd`)
- Hidden/internal command
- Args: 1 positional argument (repoRoot)
- Used by stop hook to apply pending REVIEW.md

**Wingman Review Command** (`newWingmanReviewCmd`)
- Hidden/internal command
- Args: 1 positional argument (payloadPath - path to wingman-payload.json)
- Used by detached review subprocess

### 2. **Settings Structure** (`.entire/settings.json`)

```json
{

      "model": "opus"

  }
}
```

**Model Resolution** (line 271-282):

- `wingmanReviewTimeout = 5 * time.Minute` - Claude review call timeout
- `wingmanApplyTimeout = 15 * time.Minute` - Auto-apply timeout

- **handleWingmanTurnEnd()** (line 103-132) - Triggers review after agent turn (auto-commit strategy only), calls auto-apply on pending
- **triggerWingmanReview()** (line 253-335 in wingman.go) - Main trigger function that checks preconditions and spawns detached subprocess
- **triggerWingmanFromCommit()** (line 340-408 in wingman.go) - Git post-commit hook trigger for manual-commit strategy
- **triggerWingmanAutoApplyIfPending()** (line 141-182) - Auto-apply handler called from stop hook

### 7. **How Wingman is Triggered**

**For Auto-Commit Strategy:**
- `lifecycle.go` calls `handleWingmanTurnEnd()` after SaveChanges
- Which calls `triggerWingmanReview()` with WingmanPayload

- Builds payload from HEAD commit and spawns review subprocess

- On prompt submit (`handleWingmanTurnStart`), pending review is injected

The CLI uses a consistent settings-based pattern (not CLI flags) for agent/model configuration across commands:

**Example from Setup Command** (`setup.go`, line 136):

```go
    "Agent to setup hooks for (e.g., claude-code). Enables non-interactive mode.")
```

**Settings Pattern** (used by wingman, explain --generate, summarize):
- Settings are stored in `.entire/settings.json` and `.entire/settings.local.json`
- Accessed via `settings.Load()` and helper methods like `WingmanAgent()`, `WingmanModel()`
- No command-line flags for agent/model (all configured via settings)

**Absolute Paths:**
- `/Users/dip/Repositories/cli/cmd/entire/cli/wingman.go` - Main wingman commands (581 lines)
- `/Users/dip/Repositories/cli/cmd/entire/cli/wingman_review.go` - Review subprocess logic (585 lines)
- `/Users/dip/Repositories/cli/cmd/entire/cli/wingman_lifecycle.go` - Lifecycle hooks (230 lines)
- `/Users/dip/Repositories/cli/cmd/entire/cli/wingman_prompt.go` - Review prompt building (141 lines)
- `/Users/dip/Repositories/cli/cmd/entire/cli/wingman_instruction.md` - Instructions for auto-apply
- `/Users/dip/Repositories/cli/cmd/entire/cli/settings/settings.go` - Settings loading/access (374 lines)

### Summary

Wingman doesn't use command-line flags for agent/model configuration—it reads entirely from settings files via `strategy_options.wingman.agent` and `strategy_options.wingman.model`. The default agent is "claude-code" and default model is "opus". The review and auto-apply are triggered automatically during lifecycle events (turn end for auto-commit, post-commit for manual-commit).

   252→// triggerWingmanReview checks preconditions and spawns the detached review process.
   253→func triggerWingmanReview(payload WingmanPayload) {
   254→	// Prevent infinite recursion: if we're inside a wingman auto-apply,
   255→	// don't trigger another review. The env var is set by triggerAutoApply.
   256→	if os.Getenv("ENTIRE_WINGMAN_APPLY") != "" {
   257→		return
   258→	}
   259→
   260→	logCtx := logging.WithComponent(context.Background(), "wingman")
   261→	repoRoot := payload.RepoRoot
   262→
   263→	totalFiles := len(payload.ModifiedFiles) + len(payload.NewFiles) + len(payload.DeletedFiles)
   264→	logging.Info(logCtx, "wingman trigger evaluating",
   265→		slog.String("session_id", payload.SessionID),
   266→		slog.Int("file_count", totalFiles),
   267→	)
   268→
   269→	// Check if a pending REVIEW.md already exists for the current session
   270→	if shouldSkipPendingReview(repoRoot, payload.SessionID) {
   271→		logging.Info(logCtx, "wingman skipped: pending review exists for current session")
   272→		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "[wingman] Pending review exists, skipping\n")
   273→		return
   274→	}
   275→
   276→	// Atomic lock file prevents concurrent review spawns. O_CREATE|O_EXCL
   277→	// is atomic on all platforms, avoiding the TOCTOU race of Stat+WriteFile.
   278→	lockPath := filepath.Join(repoRoot, wingmanLockFile)
   279→	if !acquireWingmanLock(lockPath, payload.SessionID) {
   280→		logging.Info(logCtx, "wingman skipped: review already in progress")
   281→		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "[wingman] Review in progress, skipping\n")
   282→		return
   283→	}
   284→
   285→	// Dedup check: compute hash of sorted file paths
   286→	allFiles := make([]string, 0, len(payload.ModifiedFiles)+len(payload.NewFiles)+len(payload.DeletedFiles))
   287→	allFiles = append(allFiles, payload.ModifiedFiles...)
   288→	allFiles = append(allFiles, payload.NewFiles...)
   289→	allFiles = append(allFiles, payload.DeletedFiles...)
   290→	filesHash := computeFilesHash(allFiles)
   291→
   292→	state, _ := loadWingmanState() //nolint:errcheck // best-effort dedup
   293→	if state != nil && state.FilesHash == filesHash && state.SessionID == payload.SessionID {
   294→		logging.Info(logCtx, "wingman skipped: dedup hash match",
   295→			slog.String("files_hash", filesHash[:12]),
   296→		)
   297→		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "[wingman] Already reviewed these changes, skipping\n")
   298→		return
   299→	}
   300→
   301→	// Capture HEAD at trigger time so the detached review diffs against
   302→	// the correct commit even if HEAD moves during the initial delay.
   303→	payload.BaseCommit = resolveHEAD(repoRoot)
   304→	logging.Debug(logCtx, "wingman captured base commit",
   305→		slog.String("base_commit", payload.BaseCommit),
   306→	)
   307→
   308→	// Write payload to a temp file instead of passing as a CLI argument,
   309→	// which can exceed OS argv limits (~128KB Linux, ~256KB macOS) with
   310→	// many files or long prompts.
   311→	payloadJSON, err := json.Marshal(payload)
   312→	if err != nil {
   313→		logging.Error(logCtx, "wingman failed to marshal payload", slog.Any("error", err))
   314→		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "[wingman] Failed to marshal payload: %v\n", err)
   315→		_ = os.Remove(lockPath)
   316→		return
   317→	}
   318→	payloadPath := filepath.Join(repoRoot, ".entire", "wingman-payload.json")
   319→	//nolint:gosec // G306: payload file is not secrets
   320→	if err := os.WriteFile(payloadPath, payloadJSON, 0o644); err != nil {
   321→		logging.Error(logCtx, "wingman failed to write payload file", slog.Any("error", err))
   322→		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "[wingman] Failed to write payload file: %v\n", err)
   323→		_ = os.Remove(lockPath)
   324→		return
   325→	}
   326→
   327→	// Spawn detached review process with path to payload file
   328→	spawnDetachedWingmanReview(repoRoot, payloadPath)
   329→	logging.Info(logCtx, "wingman review spawned",
   330→		slog.String("session_id", payload.SessionID),
   331→		slog.String("base_commit", payload.BaseCommit),
   332→		slog.Int("file_count", totalFiles),
   333→	)

   336→
   337→// triggerWingmanFromCommit builds a wingman payload from the HEAD commit and
   338→// triggers a review. Used by the git post-commit hook for manual-commit strategy
   339→// where files are committed by the user (not by SaveChanges).
   340→func triggerWingmanFromCommit() {
   341→	// Prevent infinite recursion: skip if inside wingman auto-apply
   342→	if os.Getenv("ENTIRE_WINGMAN_APPLY") != "" {
   343→		return
   344→	}
   345→	if !settings.IsWingmanEnabled() {
   346→		return
   347→	}
   348→
   349→	repoRoot, err := paths.RepoRoot()
   350→	if err != nil {
   351→		return
   352→	}
   353→
   354→	head := resolveHEAD(repoRoot)
   355→	if head == "" {
   356→		return
   357→	}
   358→
   359→	// Get changed files from the commit
   360→	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 30*time.Second)
   361→	defer cancel()
   362→	//nolint:gosec // G204: head is from git rev-parse, not user input
   363→	cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "git", "diff-tree", "--no-commit-id", "--name-status", "-r", head)
   364→	cmd.Dir = repoRoot
   365→	out, err := cmd.Output()
   366→	if err != nil || len(out) == 0 {
   367→		return
   368→	}
   369→
   370→	var modified, newFiles, deleted []string
   371→	for _, line := range strings.Split(strings.TrimSpace(string(out)), "\n") {
   372→		if len(line) < 3 {
   373→			continue
   374→		}
   375→		status := line[0]
   376→		file := strings.TrimSpace(line[1:])
   377→		switch status {
   378→		case 'M':
   379→			modified = append(modified, file)
   380→		case 'A':
   381→			newFiles = append(newFiles, file)
   382→		case 'D':
   383→			deleted = append(deleted, file)
   384→		}
   385→	}
   386→
   387→	if len(modified)+len(newFiles)+len(deleted) == 0 {
   388→		return
   389→	}
   390→
   391→	// Get commit message
   392→	//nolint:gosec // G204: head is from git rev-parse, not user input
   393→	msgCmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "git", "log", "-1", "--format=%B", head)
   394→	msgCmd.Dir = repoRoot
   395→	msgOut, _ := msgCmd.Output() //nolint:errcheck // best-effort commit message
   396→	commitMessage := strings.TrimSpace(string(msgOut))
   397→
   398→	sessionID := strategy.FindMostRecentSession()
   399→
   400→	triggerWingmanReview(WingmanPayload{
   401→		SessionID:     sessionID,
   402→		RepoRoot:      repoRoot,
   403→		ModifiedFiles: modified,
   404→		NewFiles:      newFiles,
   405→		DeletedFiles:  deleted,
   406→		CommitMessage: commitMessage,
   407→	})

   410→// staleLockThreshold is how old a lock file can be before we consider it stale
   411→// (e.g., the detached process was SIGKILLed and the defer never ran).
   412→const staleLockThreshold = 30 * time.Minute
   413→
   414→// acquireWingmanLock atomically creates the lock file. Returns true if acquired.
   415→// If the lock already exists but is older than staleLockThreshold, it is removed
   416→// and re-acquired (handles crashed detached processes).
   417→func acquireWingmanLock(lockPath, sessionID string) bool {

   452→	cmd.Dir = repoRoot

   463→	sorted := make([]string, len(files))
   464→	copy(sorted, files)
   465→	sort.Strings(sorted)
   466→	h := sha256.Sum256([]byte(strings.Join(sorted, "\x00")))

   558→	}

   564→	}

   568→		_ = os.Remove(reviewPath)
   569→		return false
   570→	}
   571→
   572→	return true // Current session, fresh review — skip

1→package agent
     2→
     3→import (
     4→	"fmt"
     5→	"slices"
     6→	"sync"
     7→)
     8→
     9→var (
    10→	registryMu sync.RWMutex
    11→	registry   = make(map[AgentName]Factory)
    12→)
    13→
    14→// Factory creates a new agent instance
    15→type Factory func() Agent
    16→
    17→// Register adds an agent factory to the registry.
    18→// Called from init() in each agent implementation.
    19→func Register(name AgentName, factory Factory) {
    20→	registryMu.Lock()
    21→	defer registryMu.Unlock()
    22→	registry[name] = factory
    23→}
    24→
    25→// Get retrieves an agent by name.
    26→//
    27→
    28→func Get(name AgentName) (Agent, error) {
    29→	registryMu.RLock()
    30→	defer registryMu.RUnlock()
    31→
    32→	factory, ok := registry[name]
    33→	if !ok {
    34→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("unknown agent: %s (available: %v)", name, List())
    35→	}
    36→	return factory(), nil
    37→}
    38→
    39→// List returns all registered agent names in sorted order.
    40→func List() []AgentName {
    41→	registryMu.RLock()
    42→	defer registryMu.RUnlock()
    43→
    44→	names := make([]AgentName, 0, len(registry))
    45→	for name := range registry {
    46→		names = append(names, name)
    47→	}
    48→	slices.Sort(names)
    49→	return names
    50→}
    51→
    52→// DetectAll returns all agents whose DetectPresence reports true.
    53→// Agents are checked in sorted name order (via List()) for deterministic results.
    54→// Returns an empty slice when no agent is detected.
    55→func DetectAll() []Agent {
    56→	names := List() // sorted, lock-safe
    57→
    58→	var detected []Agent
    59→	for _, name := range names {
    60→		ag, err := Get(name)
    61→		if err != nil {
    62→			continue
    63→		}
    64→		if present, err := ag.DetectPresence(); err == nil && present {
    65→			detected = append(detected, ag)
    66→		}
    67→	}
    68→	return detected
    69→}
    70→
    71→// Detect attempts to auto-detect which agent is being used.
    72→// Iterates registered agents in sorted name order for deterministic results.
    73→// Returns the first agent whose DetectPresence reports true.
    74→func Detect() (Agent, error) {
    75→	detected := DetectAll()
    76→	if len(detected) == 0 {
    77→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("no agent detected (available: %v)", List())
    78→	}
    79→	return detected[0], nil
    80→}
    81→
    82→// AgentName is the registry key type for agents (e.g., "claude-code", "gemini").
    83→//
    84→//nolint:revive // stuttering is intentional - distinguishes from AgentType when both are used
    85→type AgentName string
    86→
    87→// AgentType is the display name type stored in metadata/trailers (e.g., "Claude Code", "Gemini CLI").
    88→//
    89→//nolint:revive // stuttering is intentional - distinguishes from AgentName when both are used
    90→type AgentType string
    91→
    92→// Agent name constants (registry keys)
    93→const (
    94→	AgentNameClaudeCode AgentName = "claude-code"
    95→	AgentNameGemini     AgentName = "gemini"
    96→)
    97→
    98→// Agent type constants (type identifiers stored in metadata/trailers)
    99→const (
   100→	AgentTypeClaudeCode AgentType = "Claude Code"
   101→	AgentTypeGemini     AgentType = "Gemini CLI"
   102→	AgentTypeUnknown    AgentType = "Agent" // Fallback for backwards compatibility
   103→)
   104→
   105→// DefaultAgentName is the registry key for the default agent.
   106→const DefaultAgentName AgentName = AgentNameClaudeCode
   107→
   108→// GetByAgentType retrieves an agent by its type identifier.
   109→//
   110→// Note: This uses a linear search that instantiates agents until a match is found.
   111→// This is acceptable because:
   112→//   - Agent count is small (~2-20 agents)
   113→//   - Agent factories are lightweight (empty struct allocation)
   114→//   - Called infrequently (commit hooks, rewind, debug commands - not hot paths)
   115→//   - Cost is ~400ns worst case vs milliseconds for I/O operations
   116→//
   117→// Only optimize if agent count exceeds 100 or profiling shows this as a bottleneck.
   118→func GetByAgentType(agentType AgentType) (Agent, error) {
   119→	registryMu.RLock()
   120→	defer registryMu.RUnlock()
   121→
   122→	for _, factory := range registry {
   123→		ag := factory()
   124→		if ag.Type() == agentType {
   125→			return ag, nil
   126→		}
   127→	}
   128→
   129→	return nil, fmt.Errorf("unknown agent type: %s", agentType)
   130→}
   131→
   132→// AllProtectedDirs returns the union of ProtectedDirs from all registered agents.
   133→func AllProtectedDirs() []string {
   134→	// Copy factories under the lock, then release before calling external code.
   135→	registryMu.RLock()
   136→	factories := make([]Factory, 0, len(registry))
   137→	for _, f := range registry {
   138→		factories = append(factories, f)
   139→	}
   140→	registryMu.RUnlock()
   141→
   142→	seen := make(map[string]struct{})
   143→	var dirs []string
   144→	for _, factory := range factories {
   145→		for _, d := range factory().ProtectedDirs() {
   146→			if _, ok := seen[d]; !ok {
   147→				seen[d] = struct{}{}
   148→				dirs = append(dirs, d)
   149→			}
   150→		}
   151→	}
   152→	slices.Sort(dirs)
   153→	return dirs
   154→}
   155→

   157→// Returns nil if the default agent is not registered.
   158→//
   159→//nolint:errcheck // Factory pattern returns interface; error is acceptable to ignore for default
   160→func Default() Agent {
   161→	a, _ := Get(DefaultAgentName)
   162→	return a
   163→}

1→// Package agent provides interfaces and types for integrating with coding agents.
     2→// It abstracts agent-specific behavior (hooks, log parsing, session storage) so that
     3→// the same Strategy implementations can work with any coding agent.
     4→package agent
     5→
     6→import (
     7→	"io"
     8→)
     9→
    10→// Agent defines the interface for interacting with a coding agent.
    11→// Each agent implementation (Claude Code, Cursor, Aider, etc.) converts its
    12→// native format to the normalized types defined in this package.
    13→//
    14→// The interface is organized into four groups:
    15→//
    16→//   - Identity (5 methods): Name, Type, Description, DetectPresence, ProtectedDirs
    17→//   - Event Mapping (2 methods): HookNames, ParseHookEvent
    18→//   - Transcript Storage (3 methods): ReadTranscript, ChunkTranscript, ReassembleTranscript
    19→//   - Legacy (8 methods): Will be moved to optional interfaces or removed in a future phase
    20→type Agent interface {
    21→	// --- Identity ---
    22→
    23→	// Name returns the agent registry key (e.g., "claude-code", "gemini")
    24→	Name() AgentName
    25→
    26→	// Type returns the agent type identifier (e.g., "Claude Code", "Gemini CLI")
    27→	// This is stored in metadata and trailers.
    28→	Type() AgentType
    29→
    30→	// Description returns a human-readable description for UI
    31→	Description() string
    32→
    33→	// DetectPresence checks if this agent is configured in the repository
    34→	DetectPresence() (bool, error)
    35→
    36→	// ProtectedDirs returns repo-root-relative directories that should never be
    37→	// modified or deleted during rewind or other destructive operations.
    38→	// Examples: [".claude"] for Claude, [".gemini"] for Gemini.
    39→	ProtectedDirs() []string
    40→
    41→	// --- Event Mapping ---
    42→
    43→	// HookNames returns the hook verbs this agent supports.
    44→	// These become subcommands under `entire hooks <agent>`.
    45→	// e.g., ["stop", "user-prompt-submit", "session-start", "session-end"]
    46→	HookNames() []string
    47→
    48→	// ParseHookEvent translates an agent-native hook into a normalized lifecycle Event.
    49→	// Returns nil if the hook has no lifecycle significance (e.g., pass-through hooks).
    50→	// This is the core contribution surface for new agent implementations.
    51→	ParseHookEvent(hookName string, stdin io.Reader) (*Event, error)
    52→
    53→	// --- Transcript Storage ---
    54→
    55→	// ReadTranscript reads the raw transcript bytes for a session.
    56→	ReadTranscript(sessionRef string) ([]byte, error)
    57→
    58→	// ChunkTranscript splits a transcript into chunks if it exceeds maxSize.
    59→	// Returns a slice of chunks. If the transcript fits in one chunk, returns single-element slice.
    60→	// The chunking is format-aware: JSONL splits at line boundaries, JSON splits message arrays.
    61→	ChunkTranscript(content []byte, maxSize int) ([][]byte, error)
    62→
    63→	// ReassembleTranscript combines chunks back into a single transcript.
    64→	// Handles format-specific reassembly (JSONL concatenation, JSON message merging).
    65→	ReassembleTranscript(chunks [][]byte) ([]byte, error)
    66→
    67→	// --- Legacy methods (will move to optional interfaces in Phase 4) ---
    68→
    69→	// GetHookConfigPath returns path to hook config file (empty if none).
    70→	GetHookConfigPath() string
    71→
    72→	// SupportsHooks returns true if agent supports lifecycle hooks.
    73→	SupportsHooks() bool
    74→
    75→	// ParseHookInput parses hook callback input from stdin.
    76→	ParseHookInput(hookType HookType, reader io.Reader) (*HookInput, error)
    77→
    78→	// GetSessionID extracts session ID from hook input.
    79→	GetSessionID(input *HookInput) string
    80→
    81→	// GetSessionDir returns where agent stores session data for this repo.
    82→	GetSessionDir(repoPath string) (string, error)
    83→
    84→	// ResolveSessionFile returns the path to the session transcript file.
    85→	ResolveSessionFile(sessionDir, agentSessionID string) string
    86→
    87→	// ReadSession reads session data from agent's storage.
    88→	ReadSession(input *HookInput) (*AgentSession, error)
    89→
    90→	// WriteSession writes session data for resumption.
    91→	WriteSession(session *AgentSession) error
    92→
    93→	// FormatResumeCommand returns command to resume a session.
    94→	FormatResumeCommand(sessionID string) string
    95→}
    96→
    97→// HookSupport is implemented by agents with lifecycle hooks.
    98→// This optional interface allows agents like Claude Code and Cursor to
    99→// install and manage hooks that notify Entire of agent events.
   100→type HookSupport interface {
   101→	Agent
   102→
   103→	// InstallHooks installs agent-specific hooks.
   104→	// If localDev is true, hooks point to local development build.
   105→	// If force is true, removes existing Entire hooks before installing.
   106→	// Returns the number of hooks installed.
   107→	InstallHooks(localDev bool, force bool) (int, error)
   108→
   109→	// UninstallHooks removes installed hooks
   110→	UninstallHooks() error
   111→
   112→	// AreHooksInstalled checks if hooks are currently installed
   113→	AreHooksInstalled() bool
   114→
   115→	// GetSupportedHooks returns the hook types this agent supports
   116→	GetSupportedHooks() []HookType
   117→}
   118→
   119→// HookHandler is implemented by agents that define their own hook vocabulary.
   120→// HookNames() is now part of the core Agent interface.
   121→// This interface is kept for backward compatibility during migration.
   122→type HookHandler interface {
   123→	Agent
   124→
   125→	// GetHookNames returns the hook verbs this agent supports.
   126→	GetHookNames() []string
   127→}
   128→
   129→// FileWatcher is implemented by agents that use file-based detection.
   130→// Agents like Aider that don't support hooks can use file watching
   131→// to detect session activity.
   132→type FileWatcher interface {
   133→	Agent
   134→
   135→	// GetWatchPaths returns paths to watch for session changes
   136→	GetWatchPaths() ([]string, error)
   137→
   138→	// OnFileChange handles a detected file change and returns session info
   139→	OnFileChange(path string) (*SessionChange, error)
   140→}
   141→
   142→// TranscriptAnalyzer provides format-specific transcript parsing.
   143→// Agents that implement this get richer checkpoints (transcript-derived file lists,
   144→// prompts, summaries). Agents that don't still participate in the checkpoint lifecycle
   145→// via git-status-based file detection and raw transcript storage.
   146→type TranscriptAnalyzer interface {
   147→	Agent
   148→
   149→	// GetTranscriptPosition returns the current position (length) of a transcript.
   150→	// For JSONL formats (Claude Code), this is the line count.
   151→	// For JSON formats (Gemini CLI), this is the message count.
   152→	// Returns 0 if the file doesn't exist or is empty.
   153→	GetTranscriptPosition(path string) (int, error)
   154→
   155→	// ExtractModifiedFilesFromOffset extracts files modified since a given offset.
   156→	// For JSONL formats (Claude Code), offset is the starting line number.
   157→	// For JSON formats (Gemini CLI), offset is the starting message index.
   158→	// Returns:
   159→	//   - files: list of file paths modified by the agent (from Write/Edit tools)
   160→	//   - currentPosition: the current position (line count or message count)
   161→	//   - error: any error encountered during reading
   162→	ExtractModifiedFilesFromOffset(path string, startOffset int) (files []string, currentPosition int, err error)
   163→
   164→	// ExtractPrompts extracts user prompts from the transcript starting at the given offset.
   165→	ExtractPrompts(sessionRef string, fromOffset int) ([]string, error)
   166→
   167→	// ExtractSummary extracts a summary of the session from the transcript.
   168→	ExtractSummary(sessionRef string) (string, error)
   169→}
   170→
   171→// TranscriptPreparer is called before ReadTranscript to handle agent-specific
   172→// flush/sync requirements (e.g., Claude Code's async transcript writing).
   173→// The framework calls PrepareTranscript before ReadTranscript if implemented.
   174→type TranscriptPreparer interface {
   175→	Agent
   176→
   177→	// PrepareTranscript ensures the transcript is ready to read.
   178→	// For Claude Code, this waits for the async transcript flush to complete.
   179→	PrepareTranscript(sessionRef string) error
   180→}
   181→
   182→// TokenCalculator provides token usage calculation for a session.
   183→// The framework calls this during step save and checkpoint if implemented.
   184→type TokenCalculator interface {
   185→	Agent
   186→
   187→	// CalculateTokenUsage computes token usage from the transcript starting at the given offset.
   188→	CalculateTokenUsage(sessionRef string, fromOffset int) (*TokenUsage, error)
   189→}
   190→
   191→// SubagentAwareExtractor provides methods for extracting files and tokens including subagents.
   192→// Agents that support spawning subagents (like Claude Code's Task tool) should implement this
   193→// to ensure subagent contributions are included in checkpoints.
   194→type SubagentAwareExtractor interface {
   195→	Agent
   196→
   197→	// ExtractAllModifiedFiles extracts files modified by both the main agent and any spawned subagents.
   198→	// The subagentsDir parameter specifies where subagent transcripts are stored.
   199→	// Returns a deduplicated list of all modified file paths.
   200→	ExtractAllModifiedFiles(sessionRef string, fromOffset int, subagentsDir string) ([]string, error)
   201→
   202→	// CalculateTotalTokenUsage computes token usage including all spawned subagents.
   203→	// The subagentsDir parameter specifies where subagent transcripts are stored.
   204→	CalculateTotalTokenUsage(sessionRef string, fromOffset int, subagentsDir string) (*TokenUsage, error)
   205→}
   206→

# Add Agent/Model Selection to `entire wingman enable`

## Context

Wingman's agent and model are now configurable via `strategy_options.wingman.agent` and `strategy_options.wingman.model` in settings (from the Prompter interface work). However, the only way to set these is by manually editing the settings JSON. We need `entire wingman enable` to support agent/model selection through both CLI flags (for scripting) and an interactive picker (for humans).

## Plan

### Step 1: Add `--agent` and `--model` flags to `wingman enable`

**File:** `cmd/entire/cli/wingman.go` — `newWingmanEnableCmd()`

Add two new string flags:
- `--agent` — agent name (e.g., `claude-code`, `gemini`)
- `--model` — model name (e.g., `opus`, `sonnet`)

### Step 2: Add interactive agent picker when no `--agent` flag

When `--agent` is not provided and a TTY is available (use existing `canPromptInteractively()`), show an interactive single-select form listing agents that implement the `Prompter` interface.

Flow:
1. Get all registered agents via `agent.List()` + `agent.Get()`
2. Filter to those implementing `agent.Prompter` (type assertion)
3. If only one found → use it automatically (print "Using agent: Claude Code")

# Add Prompter Interface to Agent API & Configurable Wingman Agent/Model

## Context

Wingman currently hardcodes `claude` CLI with model `opus` for reviews and `claude --continue` for auto-apply. Summarization similarly hardcodes `claude` CLI with model `sonnet`. There are three places shelling out to `claude` with significant code duplication:

- `wingmanStripGitEnv()` and `stripGitEnv()` are identical functions in two files
- `wingmanCLIResponse` and `claudeCLIResponse` are identical structs
- exec error handling is duplicated verbatim

**Goal:** Add a `Prompter` optional interface to the Agent API so wingman and summarize can invoke any registered agent with a prompt, with agent and model configurable via settings.

## Plan

### Step 1: Create shared CLI helpers — `agent/cli_helpers.go`

New file: `cmd/entire/cli/agent/cli_helpers.go`

- `CLIResponse` struct — replaces both `wingmanCLIResponse` and `claudeCLIResponse`
- `StripGitEnv(env []string) []string` — consolidates the identical functions
- `FormatExecError(err error, cliName, stderr string) error` — consolidates duplicated error handling

New file: `cmd/entire/cli/agent/cli_helpers_test.go`
- Migrate tests from `wingman_test.go:TestWingmanStripGitEnv` and `summarize/claude_test.go:TestStripGitEnv`

### Step 2: Create Prompter interface — `agent/prompter.go`

New file: `cmd/entire/cli/agent/prompter.go`

```go
type PromptOptions struct {
    Model          string   // Override model (empty = agent default)
    WorkDir        string   // Working directory (empty = os.TempDir())
    AllowedTools   string   // Tool restriction (e.g., "Read,Glob,Grep")
    PermissionMode string   // e.g., "bypassPermissions", "acceptEdits"
    OutputFormat   string   // e.g., "json", "text" (default: "json")
    IsolateFromGit *bool    // Strip GIT_* env vars (default: true)
    ExtraEnv       []string // Additional env vars
}

type PromptResult struct {
    Text string
}

type Prompter interface {
    Agent
    Prompt(ctx context.Context, prompt string, opts PromptOptions) (*PromptResult, error)
    CLICommand() string
}
```

Follows the existing optional interface pattern (`TranscriptAnalyzer`, `TokenCalculator`, etc.).

### Step 3: Implement Prompter for Claude Code — `agent/claudecode/prompter.go`

New file: `cmd/entire/cli/agent/claudecode/prompter.go`

- Add `CommandRunner` field to `ClaudeCodeAgent` for test injection (same pattern as `summarize.ClaudeGenerator`)
- Implement `Prompt()` — builds `claude --print --setting-sources "" ...` command from PromptOptions, parses JSON response via `agent.CLIResponse`
- Implement `CLICommand()` — returns `"claude"`
- Compile-time assertion: `var _ agent.Prompter = (*ClaudeCodeAgent)(nil)`

New file: `cmd/entire/cli/agent/claudecode/prompter_test.go`
- Test with `CommandRunner` injection (mock CLI responses)

### Step 4: Add settings helpers — `settings/settings.go`

Add methods to `EntireSettings`:
- `WingmanAgent() string` — reads `strategy_options.wingman.agent`, defaults to `""`
- `WingmanModel() string` — reads `strategy_options.wingman.model`, defaults to `""`
- `SummarizeAgent() string` — reads `strategy_options.summarize.agent`, defaults to `""`
- `SummarizeModel() string` — reads `strategy_options.summarize.model`, defaults to `""`

Settings JSON example:
```json
{
  "strategy_options": {
    "wingman": { "enabled": true, "agent": "claude-code", "model": "opus" },
    "summarize": { "enabled": true, "agent": "claude-code", "model": "sonnet" }
  }
}
```

All new fields optional with backward-compatible defaults.

### Step 5: Refactor wingman review to use Prompter — `wingman_review.go`

Modify `callClaudeForReview()` → `callAgentForReview()`:
1. Load settings, get `WingmanAgent()` (default: `agent.DefaultAgentName` = "claude-code")
2. Get agent from registry, assert `agent.Prompter` interface
3. Call `prompter.Prompt(ctx, prompt, PromptOptions{Model, WorkDir: repoRoot, AllowedTools: "Read,Glob,Grep", PermissionMode: "bypassPermissions"})`

Remove:
- `wingmanCLIResponse` struct (now `agent.CLIResponse` inside Prompter)
- `wingmanStripGitEnv()` function (now `agent.StripGitEnv()` inside Prompter)
- `wingmanReviewModel` constant (now from settings with `"opus"` default)

Keep as-is:
- `triggerAutoApply()` — uses `--continue` which is not a prompt-and-response pattern; stays as direct CLI invocation but uses `agent.StripGitEnv()` instead of `wingmanStripGitEnv()`

### Step 6: Refactor summarize to use Prompter — `summarize/claude.go`

Add `PrompterGenerator` struct implementing `Generator`:
```go
type PrompterGenerator struct {
    Prompter agent.Prompter
    Model    string
}
```

Update `GenerateFromTranscript()` nil-generator fallback:
- Load settings, get `SummarizeAgent()` / `SummarizeModel()`
- Construct `PrompterGenerator` with resolved Prompter

Remove from `claude.go`:
- `stripGitEnv()` — replaced by `agent.StripGitEnv()` inside Prompter
- `claudeCLIResponse` — replaced by `agent.CLIResponse` inside Prompter

Keep `ClaudeGenerator` for backward compatibility (tests use `CommandRunner` injection).

### Step 7: Update call sites

These already pass `nil` as generator, so they get the new default behavior automatically:
- `strategy/manual_commit_condensation.go:203` — `GenerateFromTranscript(..., nil)`
- `explain.go:323` — `GenerateFromTranscript(..., nil)`

### Step 8: Non-claude agent handling

- If wingman agent is not `"claude-code"`, `triggerAutoApply` should be skipped (log a message). The `--continue` flag is Claude-specific.
- If an agent doesn't implement `Prompter`, return clear error: `"agent X does not support prompting"`
- Gemini Prompter can be added later when needed — for now only Claude Code implements it.

## Files Modified

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `cmd/entire/cli/agent/cli_helpers.go` | **New** — `CLIResponse`, `StripGitEnv`, `FormatExecError` |
| `cmd/entire/cli/agent/cli_helpers_test.go` | **New** — tests |
| `cmd/entire/cli/agent/prompter.go` | **New** — `Prompter` interface, `PromptOptions`, `PromptResult` |
| `cmd/entire/cli/agent/claudecode/claude.go` | Add `CommandRunner` field to struct |
| `cmd/entire/cli/agent/claudecode/prompter.go` | **New** — `Prompt()`, `CLICommand()` implementation |
| `cmd/entire/cli/agent/claudecode/prompter_test.go` | **New** — tests |
| `cmd/entire/cli/settings/settings.go` | Add `WingmanAgent/Model`, `SummarizeAgent/Model` methods |
| `cmd/entire/cli/wingman_review.go` | Use Prompter; remove `wingmanCLIResponse`, `wingmanStripGitEnv`, `wingmanReviewModel` |
| `cmd/entire/cli/wingman_test.go` | Update: remove `TestWingmanStripGitEnv`, update review tests |
| `cmd/entire/cli/summarize/claude.go` | Add `PrompterGenerator`; remove `stripGitEnv`, `claudeCLIResponse` |
| `cmd/entire/cli/summarize/summarize.go` | Update nil-generator fallback to use `PrompterGenerator` |
| `cmd/entire/cli/summarize/claude_test.go` | Update: remove `TestStripGitEnv`, add `PrompterGenerator` tests |

## Verification

```bash
mise run fmt && mise run lint && mise run test:ci
```

Manually verify:
1. Enable wingman without agent/model in settings → defaults to claude-code + opus
2. Set `"agent": "claude-code", "model": "sonnet"` in wingman settings → uses sonnet
3. Summarize still works with nil generator → resolves from settings
4. `triggerAutoApply` still works (not refactored to Prompter)

- `--model` — model name (e.g., `opus`, `sonnet`)

- If interactive: show `huh.NewInput` text field pre-filled with `"opus"` (the wingman default)
- If no TTY: use default model silently

- Test enable without flags in non-interactive mode → verify defaults used
- Test enable with invalid agent name → verify error
- Test enable with agent that doesn't implement Prompter → verify error
- Test status shows agent/model when configured

| `cmd/entire/cli/wingman_test.go` | Add tests for new flags and status output |

```bash
mise run fmt && mise run lint && mise run test:ci
```

# Add Prompter Interface to Agent API & Configurable Wingman Agent/Model

## Context

Wingman currently hardcodes `claude` CLI with model `opus` for reviews and `claude --continue` for auto-apply. Summarization similarly hardcodes `claude` CLI with model `sonnet`. There are three places shelling out to `claude` with significant code duplication:

- `wingmanStripGitEnv()` and `stripGitEnv()` are identical functions in two files
- `wingmanCLIResponse` and `claudeCLIResponse` are identical structs
- exec error handling is duplicated verbatim

**Goal:** Add a `Prompter` optional interface to the Agent API so wingman and summarize can invoke any registered agent with a prompt, with agent and model configurable via settings.

## Plan

### Step 1: Create shared CLI helpers — `agent/cli_helpers.go`

New file: `cmd/entire/cli/agent/cli_helpers.go`

- `CLIResponse` struct — replaces both `wingmanCLIResponse` and `claudeCLIResponse`
- `StripGitEnv(env []string) []string` — consolidates the identical functions
- `FormatExecError(err error, cliName, stderr string) error` — consolidates duplicated error handling

New file: `cmd/entire/cli/agent/cli_helpers_test.go`
- Migrate tests from `wingman_test.go:TestWingmanStripGitEnv` and `summarize/claude_test.go:TestStripGitEnv`

### Step 2: Create Prompter interface — `agent/prompter.go`

New file: `cmd/entire/cli/agent/prompter.go`

```go
type PromptOptions struct {
    Model          string   // Override model (empty = agent default)
    WorkDir        string   // Working directory (empty = os.TempDir())
    AllowedTools   string   // Tool restriction (e.g., "Read,Glob,Grep")
    PermissionMode string   // e.g., "bypassPermissions", "acceptEdits"
    OutputFormat   string   // e.g., "json", "text" (default: "json")
    IsolateFromGit *bool    // Strip GIT_* env vars (default: true)
    ExtraEnv       []string // Additional env vars
}

type PromptResult struct {
    Text string
}

type Prompter interface {
    Agent
    Prompt(ctx context.Context, prompt string, opts PromptOptions) (*PromptResult, error)
    CLICommand() string
}
```

Follows the existing optional interface pattern (`TranscriptAnalyzer`, `TokenCalculator`, etc.).

### Step 3: Implement Prompter for Claude Code — `agent/claudecode/prompter.go`

New file: `cmd/entire/cli/agent/claudecode/prompter.go`

- Add `CommandRunner` field to `ClaudeCodeAgent` for test injection (same pattern as `summarize.ClaudeGenerator`)
- Implement `Prompt()` — builds `claude --print --setting-sources "" ...` command from PromptOptions, parses JSON response via `agent.CLIResponse`
- Implement `CLICommand()` — returns `"claude"`
- Compile-time assertion: `var _ agent.Prompter = (*ClaudeCodeAgent)(nil)`

New file: `cmd/entire/cli/agent/claudecode/prompter_test.go`
- Test with `CommandRunner` injection (mock CLI responses)

### Step 4: Add settings helpers — `settings/settings.go`

Add methods to `EntireSettings`:
- `WingmanAgent() string` — reads `strategy_options.wingman.agent`, defaults to `""`
- `WingmanModel() string` — reads `strategy_options.wingman.model`, defaults to `""`
- `SummarizeAgent() string` — reads `strategy_options.summarize.agent`, defaults to `""`
- `SummarizeModel() string` — reads `strategy_options.summarize.model`, defaults to `""`

Settings JSON example:
```json
{
  "strategy_options": {
    "wingman": { "enabled": true, "agent": "claude-code", "model": "opus" },
    "summarize": { "enabled": true, "agent": "claude-code", "model": "sonnet" }
  }
}
```

All new fields optional with backward-compatible defaults.

### Step 5: Refactor wingman review to use Prompter — `wingman_review.go`

Modify `callClaudeForReview()` → `callAgentForReview()`:
1. Load settings, get `WingmanAgent()` (default: `agent.DefaultAgentName` = "claude-code")
2. Get agent from registry, assert `agent.Prompter` interface
3. Call `prompter.Prompt(ctx, prompt, PromptOptions{Model, WorkDir: repoRoot, AllowedTools: "Read,Glob,Grep", PermissionMode: "bypassPermissions"})`

Remove:
- `wingmanCLIResponse` struct (now `agent.CLIResponse` inside Prompter)
- `wingmanStripGitEnv()` function (now `agent.StripGitEnv()` inside Prompter)
- `wingmanReviewModel` constant (now from settings with `"opus"` default)

Keep as-is:
- `triggerAutoApply()` — uses `--continue` which is not a prompt-and-response pattern; stays as direct CLI invocation but uses `agent.StripGitEnv()` instead of `wingmanStripGitEnv()`

### Step 6: Refactor summarize to use Prompter — `summarize/claude.go`

Add `PrompterGenerator` struct implementing `Generator`:
```go
type PrompterGenerator struct {
    Prompter agent.Prompter
    Model    string
}
```

Update `GenerateFromTranscript()` nil-generator fallback:
- Load settings, get `SummarizeAgent()` / `SummarizeModel()`
- Construct `PrompterGenerator` with resolved Prompter

Remove from `claude.go`:
- `stripGitEnv()` — replaced by `agent.StripGitEnv()` inside Prompter
- `claudeCLIResponse` — replaced by `agent.CLIResponse` inside Prompter

Keep `ClaudeGenerator` for backward compatibility (tests use `CommandRunner` injection).

### Step 7: Update call sites

These already pass `nil` as generator, so they get the new default behavior automatically:
- `strategy/manual_commit_condensation.go:203` — `GenerateFromTranscript(..., nil)`
- `explain.go:323` — `GenerateFromTranscript(..., nil)`

### Step 8: Non-claude agent handling

- If wingman agent is not `"claude-code"`, `triggerAutoApply` should be skipped (log a message). The `--continue` flag is Claude-specific.
- If an agent doesn't implement `Prompter`, return clear error: `"agent X does not support prompting"`
- Gemini Prompter can be added later when needed — for now only Claude Code implements it.

## Files Modified

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `cmd/entire/cli/agent/cli_helpers.go` | **New** — `CLIResponse`, `StripGitEnv`, `FormatExecError` |
| `cmd/entire/cli/agent/cli_helpers_test.go` | **New** — tests |
| `cmd/entire/cli/agent/prompter.go` | **New** — `Prompter` interface, `PromptOptions`, `PromptResult` |
| `cmd/entire/cli/agent/claudecode/claude.go` | Add `CommandRunner` field to struct |
| `cmd/entire/cli/agent/claudecode/prompter.go` | **New** — `Prompt()`, `CLICommand()` implementation |
| `cmd/entire/cli/agent/claudecode/prompter_test.go` | **New** — tests |
| `cmd/entire/cli/settings/settings.go` | Add `WingmanAgent/Model`, `SummarizeAgent/Model` methods |
| `cmd/entire/cli/wingman_review.go` | Use Prompter; remove `wingmanCLIResponse`, `wingmanStripGitEnv`, `wingmanReviewModel` |
| `cmd/entire/cli/wingman_test.go` | Update: remove `TestWingmanStripGitEnv`, update review tests |
| `cmd/entire/cli/summarize/claude.go` | Add `PrompterGenerator`; remove `stripGitEnv`, `claudeCLIResponse` |
| `cmd/entire/cli/summarize/summarize.go` | Update nil-generator fallback to use `PrompterGenerator` |
| `cmd/entire/cli/summarize/claude_test.go` | Update: remove `TestStripGitEnv`, add `PrompterGenerator` tests |

## Verification

```bash
mise run fmt && mise run lint && mise run test:ci
```

Manually verify:
1. Enable wingman without agent/model in settings → defaults to claude-code + opus
2. Set `"agent": "claude-code", "model": "sonnet"` in wingman settings → uses sonnet
3. Summarize still works with nil generator → resolves from settings
4. `triggerAutoApply` still works (not refactored to Prompter)

   252→// triggerWingmanReview checks preconditions and spawns the detached review process.
   253→func triggerWingmanReview(payload WingmanPayload) {
   254→	// Prevent infinite recursion: if we're inside a wingman auto-apply,
   255→	// don't trigger another review. The env var is set by triggerAutoApply.
   256→	if os.Getenv("ENTIRE_WINGMAN_APPLY") != "" {
   257→		return
   258→	}
   259→
   260→	logCtx := logging.WithComponent(context.Background(), "wingman")
   261→	repoRoot := payload.RepoRoot
   262→
   263→	totalFiles := len(payload.ModifiedFiles) + len(payload.NewFiles) + len(payload.DeletedFiles)
   264→	logging.Info(logCtx, "wingman trigger evaluating",
   265→		slog.String("session_id", payload.SessionID),
   266→		slog.Int("file_count", totalFiles),
   267→	)
   268→
   269→	// Check if a pending REVIEW.md already exists for the current session
   270→	if shouldSkipPendingReview(repoRoot, payload.SessionID) {
   271→		logging.Info(logCtx, "wingman skipped: pending review exists for current session")
   272→		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "[wingman] Pending review exists, skipping\n")
   273→		return
   274→	}
   275→
   276→	// Atomic lock file prevents concurrent review spawns. O_CREATE|O_EXCL
   277→	// is atomic on all platforms, avoiding the TOCTOU race of Stat+WriteFile.
   278→	lockPath := filepath.Join(repoRoot, wingmanLockFile)
   279→	if !acquireWingmanLock(lockPath, payload.SessionID) {
   280→		logging.Info(logCtx, "wingman skipped: review already in progress")
   281→		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "[wingman] Review in progress, skipping\n")
   282→		return
   283→	}
   284→
   285→	// Dedup check: compute hash of sorted file paths
   286→	allFiles := make([]string, 0, len(payload.ModifiedFiles)+len(payload.NewFiles)+len(payload.DeletedFiles))
   287→	allFiles = append(allFiles, payload.ModifiedFiles...)
   288→	allFiles = append(allFiles, payload.NewFiles...)
   289→	allFiles = append(allFiles, payload.DeletedFiles...)
   290→	filesHash := computeFilesHash(allFiles)
   291→
   292→	state, _ := loadWingmanState() //nolint:errcheck // best-effort dedup
   293→	if state != nil && state.FilesHash == filesHash && state.SessionID == payload.SessionID {
   294→		logging.Info(logCtx, "wingman skipped: dedup hash match",
   295→			slog.String("files_hash", filesHash[:12]),
   296→		)
   297→		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "[wingman] Already reviewed these changes, skipping\n")
   298→		return
   299→	}
   300→
   301→	// Capture HEAD at trigger time so the detached review diffs against
   302→	// the correct commit even if HEAD moves during the initial delay.
   303→	payload.BaseCommit = resolveHEAD(repoRoot)
   304→	logging.Debug(logCtx, "wingman captured base commit",
   305→		slog.String("base_commit", payload.BaseCommit),
   306→	)
   307→
   308→	// Write payload to a temp file instead of passing as a CLI argument,
   309→	// which can exceed OS argv limits (~128KB Linux, ~256KB macOS) with
   310→	// many files or long prompts.
   311→	payloadJSON, err := json.Marshal(payload)
   312→	if err != nil {
   313→		logging.Error(logCtx, "wingman failed to marshal payload", slog.Any("error", err))
   314→		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "[wingman] Failed to marshal payload: %v\n", err)
   315→		_ = os.Remove(lockPath)
   316→		return
   317→	}
   318→	payloadPath := filepath.Join(repoRoot, ".entire", "wingman-payload.json")
   319→	//nolint:gosec // G306: payload file is not secrets
   320→	if err := os.WriteFile(payloadPath, payloadJSON, 0o644); err != nil {
   321→		logging.Error(logCtx, "wingman failed to write payload file", slog.Any("error", err))
   322→		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "[wingman] Failed to write payload file: %v\n", err)
   323→		_ = os.Remove(lockPath)
   324→		return
   325→	}
   326→
   327→	// Spawn detached review process with path to payload file
   328→	spawnDetachedWingmanReview(repoRoot, payloadPath)
   329→	logging.Info(logCtx, "wingman review spawned",
   330→		slog.String("session_id", payload.SessionID),
   331→		slog.String("base_commit", payload.BaseCommit),
   332→		slog.Int("file_count", totalFiles),
   333→	)
   334→	fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "[wingman] Review starting in background...\n")
   335→}
