   337→// triggerWingmanFromCommit builds a wingman payload from the HEAD commit and
   338→// triggers a review. Used by the git post-commit hook for manual-commit strategy
   339→// where files are committed by the user (not by SaveChanges).
   340→func triggerWingmanFromCommit() {
   341→	// Prevent infinite recursion: skip if inside wingman auto-apply
   342→	if os.Getenv("ENTIRE_WINGMAN_APPLY") != "" {
   343→		return
   344→	}
   345→	if !settings.IsWingmanEnabled() {
   346→		return
   347→	}
   348→
   349→	repoRoot, err := paths.RepoRoot()
   350→	if err != nil {
   351→		return
   352→	}
   353→
   354→	head := resolveHEAD(repoRoot)
   355→	if head == "" {
   356→		return
   357→	}
   358→
   359→	// Get changed files from the commit
   360→	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 30*time.Second)
   361→	defer cancel()
   362→	//nolint:gosec // G204: head is from git rev-parse, not user input
   363→	cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "git", "diff-tree", "--no-commit-id", "--name-status", "-r", head)
   364→	cmd.Dir = repoRoot
   365→	out, err := cmd.Output()
   366→	if err != nil || len(out) == 0 {
   367→		return
   368→	}
   369→
   370→	var modified, newFiles, deleted []string
   371→	for _, line := range strings.Split(strings.TrimSpace(string(out)), "\n") {
   372→		if len(line) < 3 {
   373→			continue
   374→		}
   375→		status := line[0]
   376→		file := strings.TrimSpace(line[1:])
   377→		switch status {
   378→		case 'M':
   379→			modified = append(modified, file)
   380→		case 'A':
   381→			newFiles = append(newFiles, file)
   382→		case 'D':
   383→			deleted = append(deleted, file)
   384→		}
   385→	}
   386→
   387→	if len(modified)+len(newFiles)+len(deleted) == 0 {
   388→		return
   389→	}
   390→
   391→	// Get commit message
   392→	//nolint:gosec // G204: head is from git rev-parse, not user input
   393→	msgCmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "git", "log", "-1", "--format=%B", head)
   394→	msgCmd.Dir = repoRoot
   395→	msgOut, _ := msgCmd.Output() //nolint:errcheck // best-effort commit message
   396→	commitMessage := strings.TrimSpace(string(msgOut))
   397→
   398→	sessionID := strategy.FindMostRecentSession()
   399→
   400→	triggerWingmanReview(WingmanPayload{
   401→		SessionID:     sessionID,
   402→		RepoRoot:      repoRoot,
   403→		ModifiedFiles: modified,
   404→		NewFiles:      newFiles,
   405→		DeletedFiles:  deleted,
   406→		CommitMessage: commitMessage,
   407→	})
   408→}
   409→
   410→// staleLockThreshold is how old a lock file can be before we consider it stale
   411→// (e.g., the detached process was SIGKILLed and the defer never ran).
   412→const staleLockThreshold = 30 * time.Minute
   413→
   414→// acquireWingmanLock atomically creates the lock file. Returns true if acquired.
   415→// If the lock already exists but is older than staleLockThreshold, it is removed
   416→// and re-acquired (handles crashed detached processes).
   417→func acquireWingmanLock(lockPath, sessionID string) bool {
   418→	//nolint:gosec // G304: lockPath is constructed from repoRoot + constant
   419→	f, err := os.OpenFile(lockPath, os.O_WRONLY|os.O_CREATE|os.O_EXCL, 0o644)
   420→	if err != nil {
   421→		if !errors.Is(err, os.ErrExist) {
   422→			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "[wingman] Failed to create lock: %v\n", err)
   423→			return false
   424→		}
   425→		// Lock exists — check if it's stale
   426→		info, statErr := os.Stat(lockPath)
   427→		if statErr != nil || time.Since(info.ModTime()) <= staleLockThreshold {
   428→			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "[wingman] Review already in progress, skipping\n")
   429→			return false
   430→		}
   431→		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "[wingman] Removing stale lock (age: %s)\n",
   432→			time.Since(info.ModTime()).Round(time.Second))
   433→		_ = os.Remove(lockPath)
   434→		// Retry the atomic create
   435→		//nolint:gosec // G304: lockPath is constructed from repoRoot + constant
   436→		f, err = os.OpenFile(lockPath, os.O_WRONLY|os.O_CREATE|os.O_EXCL, 0o644)
   437→		if err != nil {
   438→			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "[wingman] Failed to create lock after stale removal: %v\n", err)
   439→			return false
   440→		}
   441→	}
   442→	_, _ = f.WriteString(sessionID) //nolint:errcheck // best-effort session ID write
   443→	_ = f.Close()
   444→	return true
   445→}

   447→// resolveHEAD returns the current HEAD commit hash, or empty string on error.
   448→func resolveHEAD(repoRoot string) string {
   449→	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 5*time.Second)
   450→	defer cancel()
   451→	cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "git", "rev-parse", "HEAD")
   452→	cmd.Dir = repoRoot
   453→	out, err := cmd.Output()
   454→	if err != nil {
   455→		return ""
   456→	}
   457→	return strings.TrimSpace(string(out))
   458→}

   460→// computeFilesHash returns a SHA256 hex digest of the sorted file paths.
   461→// Uses null byte separator (impossible in filenames) to avoid ambiguity.
   462→func computeFilesHash(files []string) string {
   463→	sorted := make([]string, len(files))
   464→	copy(sorted, files)
   465→	sort.Strings(sorted)
   466→	h := sha256.Sum256([]byte(strings.Join(sorted, "\x00")))
   467→	return hex.EncodeToString(h[:])
   468→}

   541→// shouldSkipPendingReview checks whether a pending REVIEW.md should prevent
   542→// a new review from being triggered. It cleans up stale/orphaned reviews.
   543→//
   544→// Returns true only when REVIEW.md exists AND belongs to the current session
   545→// AND is younger than wingmanStaleReviewTTL.
   546→func shouldSkipPendingReview(repoRoot, currentSessionID string) bool {
   547→	reviewPath := filepath.Join(repoRoot, wingmanReviewFile)
   548→	if _, err := os.Stat(reviewPath); err != nil {
   549→		return false // No REVIEW.md, don't skip
   550→	}
   551→
   552→	// REVIEW.md exists — check state to determine if it's current or stale
   553→	state := loadWingmanStateDirect(repoRoot)
   554→	if state == nil {
   555→		// Orphan: REVIEW.md without state file — clean up
   556→		_ = os.Remove(reviewPath)
   557→		return false
   558→	}
   559→
   560→	if state.SessionID != currentSessionID {
   561→		// Different session — stale review, clean up
   562→		_ = os.Remove(reviewPath)
   563→		return false
   564→	}
   565→
   566→	if time.Since(state.ReviewedAt) > wingmanStaleReviewTTL {
   567→		// Same session but too old — clean up
   568→		_ = os.Remove(reviewPath)
   569→		return false
   570→	}
   571→
   572→	return true // Current session, fresh review — skip
   573→}

content.text:
All done. Here's a summary of what was changed:

**`cmd/entire/cli/wingman.go`** — `newWingmanEnableCmd()` now has:
- `--agent` flag — specify agent by name (e.g., `--agent claude-code`)
- `--model` flag — specify model (e.g., `--model sonnet`)
- Interactive picker when no flags given: detects agents implementing `Prompter`, shows a `huh.NewSelect` for agent and model
- Non-interactive fallback (no TTY): uses defaults silently
- Validation: rejects unknown agents and agents that don't implement `Prompter`

**`newWingmanStatusCmd()`** now shows:
```
Wingman: enabled
Agent: claude-code
Model: opus
```

**Helper functions added:**
- `resolveWingmanEnableAgent()` — validates flag or shows picker
- `resolveWingmanEnableModel()` — validates flag or shows picker
- `findPrompterAgents()` — filters registry to Prompter-implementing agents

**`cmd/entire/cli/wingman_test.go`** — 8 new tests covering flag validation, non-interactive defaults, and settings persistence.

**`.golangci.yaml`** — Added `summarize.Generator` to `ireturn.allow` list (replaces fragile nolint directive that `fix: true` mode kept stripping).

1→Now I understand the full picture. The `ParseFromFileAtLine` uses 0-indexed startLine and the callers in `CalculateTokenUsageFromFile` and `CalculateTotalTokenUsage` pass `startLine` directly from `GetTranscriptPosition`. Let me verify the old code used the same convention:
     2→
     3→The old `parseTranscriptFromLine` (now removed) compared `lineNum < startLine` and incremented lineNum first. So if startLine=3, it would skip lines 0, 1, 2 (0-indexed). The new `ParseFromFileAtLine` checks `totalLines >= startLine` — for startLine=3, it processes when totalLines is 3, 4, ... So both skip the first 3 lines (0, 1, 2). They're consistent.
     4→
     5→Now `GetTranscriptPosition` returns the count of lines. If there are 3 lines, it returns 3. Passing that as startLine=3 to `ParseFromFileAtLine` would skip lines 0, 1, 2 and start from line 3 — correct for incremental parsing.
     6→
     7→The `ExtractModifiedFilesFromOffset` increments `lineNum` then checks `lineNum > startOffset`. If startOffset=3, lineNum must be 4+ to process. So it also skips 3 lines. Consistent.
     8→
     9→Good, no off-by-one issue there.

Now I understand the full picture. The `ParseFromFileAtLine` uses 0-indexed startLine and the callers in `CalculateTokenUsageFromFile` and `CalculateTotalTokenUsage` pass `startLine` directly from `GetTranscriptPosition`. Let me verify the old code used the same convention:

The old `parseTranscriptFromLine` (now removed) compared `lineNum < startLine` and incremented lineNum first. So if startLine=3, it would skip lines 0, 1, 2 (0-indexed). The new `ParseFromFileAtLine` checks `totalLines >= startLine` — for startLine=3, it processes when totalLines is 3, 4, ... So both skip the first 3 lines (0, 1, 2). They're consistent.

Now `GetTranscriptPosition` returns the count of lines. If there are 3 lines, it returns 3. Passing that as startLine=3 to `ParseFromFileAtLine` would skip lines 0, 1, 2 and start from line 3 — correct for incremental parsing.

The `ExtractModifiedFilesFromOffset` increments `lineNum` then checks `lineNum > startOffset`. If startOffset=3, lineNum must be 4+ to process. So it also skips 3 lines. Consistent.

**Review addressed:** Fixed the shell injection concern in `prompter_test.go` — inlined the JSON response directly in the printf command instead of concatenating a variable into a shell string. The other review items were about pre-existing code outside this PR's scope (hook parsing, dead structs, interface docs).

---

Now to your question: you're asking if, after the wingman review completes, we could automatically prompt the main agent session (e.g., Claude Code) to address the review without the user having to type anything — essentially a 20-second timeout that auto-triggers a prompt.

The short answer is **no, not with the current architecture**. Here's why:

1. **Claude Code has no external prompt injection API** — there's no way to programmatically send a message into a running Claude Code session from outside. The `--continue` flag starts a *new* subprocess that continues the conversation, but it can't poke a live session.

2. **The current auto-apply flow** (`triggerAutoApply`) already uses `claude --continue` — but it runs as a *separate detached process*, not inside the user's interactive session. It works, but the user doesn't see it happening in their terminal.

3. **What IS possible today:** The stop hook (`handleWingmanTurnEnd`) already triggers auto-apply when a review is pending. The `SessionStart` hook injects the review as `additionalContext` on the next prompt. So the review *does* get surfaced automatically — just on the next user interaction.

To get true "auto-prompt after 20s of idle", you'd need either:
- A Claude Code plugin/MCP extension that can inject prompts into a running session (doesn't exist)
- A terminal automation approach (sending keystrokes to the terminal — fragile and platform-specific)
- Changes to Claude Code itself to support an external trigger mechanism

The closest feasible approach would be making the auto-apply (`claude --continue`) more aggressive — reducing its trigger conditions so it fires sooner. But it still runs as a separate process, not in the user's visible session.

# Ralph Wiggum Plugin Overview

The Ralph Wiggum plugin implements an iterative AI development loop for Claude Code. Here's how it works:

## Core Mechanism

**Ralph is a self-referential feedback loop** that uses a **Stop hook** to intercept Claude's exit attempts and re-prompt with the same task:

```bash
# You run ONCE:
/ralph-loop "Your task description" --completion-promise "DONE"

# Then Claude Code automatically:
# 1. Works on the task
# 2. Tries to exit
# 3. Stop hook blocks exit
# 4. Stop hook feeds the SAME prompt back
# 5. Repeat until completion
```

## How It Works

The loop operates **inside your current session** (no external bash loops needed). The key features:

- **The prompt never changes** between iterations
- Claude's **previous work persists in files**
- Each iteration sees **modified files and git history**
- Claude **autonomously improves** by reading its own past work
- Loop continues until the **completion promise is output**

## Commands

### `/ralph-loop`
```bash
/ralph-loop "<prompt>" --max-iterations <n> --completion-promise "<text>"
```

**Options:**
- `--max-iterations <n>` - Stop after N iterations (default: unlimited)
- `--completion-promise <text>` - Phrase that signals completion

### `/cancel-ralph`
Cancels the active Ralph loop.

## Example Usage

```bash
/ralph-loop "Build a REST API for todos. Requirements: CRUD operations, input validation, tests. Output <promise>COMPLETE</promise> when done." --completion-promise "COMPLETE" --max-iterations 50
```

Claude will iteratively:
1. Implement the API
2. Run tests and see failures
3. Fix bugs based on test output
4. Iterate until all requirements met

## Philosophy

- **Iteration > Perfection**: Don't aim for perfect on first try
- **Failures Are Data**: Use predictable failures to tune prompts
- **Operator Skill Matters**: Success depends on writing good prompts
- **Persistence Wins**: The loop handles retry logic automatically

## Best Practices

✅ **Clear completion criteria** with testable conditions
✅ **Incremental goals** broken into phases
✅ **Self-correction** via TDD (write tests → implement → verify → fix)
✅ **Escape hatches** using `--max-iterations` as safety net

The plugin is ideal for well-defined, iterative tasks with automatic verification (tests, linters) where you can walk away and let the loop refine the work.

That's the key insight — **Ralph uses the Stop hook**. It's exactly what we already have access to.

Here's how it works and how we could adapt it for wingman:

**Ralph's trick:** When Claude Code finishes a turn and tries to stop, the Stop hook fires. Ralph intercepts that, checks if the task is done (via a "completion promise"), and if not, **feeds the same prompt back** — causing Claude Code to start another turn automatically. The user never has to type anything.

**For wingman auto-apply, this means:** Instead of spawning a separate `claude --continue` process (which runs outside the user's session), we could use the **Stop hook response** to inject the review as the next prompt. Claude Code would then automatically start a new turn to address the review — all within the same session, visible to the user.

The flow would be:
1. Agent finishes turn → Stop hook fires
2. Stop hook sees pending `REVIEW.md` → returns it as the next prompt via hook response
3. Claude Code automatically starts a new turn to address the review
4. No 20-second timeout needed — it's immediate

This is fundamentally different from the current approach of `claude --continue` in a detached process. Want me to explore adapting the wingman auto-apply to use the Stop hook's re-prompt mechanism instead?

- Review not ready yet → re-prompt with "wait" → agent says "ok waiting" → tries to stop → Stop hook fires again

The real issue is that hooks are event-driven but we need to react to an async file-system event that doesn't map to any hook. I'm weighing the tradeoffs: a polling loop wastes resources, sleeping in the hook blocks Claude Code from exiting cleanly, accepting the current UX means reviews appear on the next interaction, or we could try a hybrid approach where the Stop hook waits briefly (maybe 30 seconds) to catch reviews that complete quickly, then lets the session end normally if nothing appears.

content.text:
Yeah, you've nailed the fundamental problem. The Stop hook is the only re-entry point, so you'd end up with a polling loop:

```
Agent finishes → Stop hook fires → review not ready → re-prompt "wait"
→ agent says "ok" → Stop hook fires → review still not ready → re-prompt "wait"
→ ... (burning API calls for minutes)
→ review lands → inject it
```

That's expensive and ugly. A few alternatives worth considering:

**1. Stop hook with a blocking wait** — instead of re-prompting, the hook script itself sleeps and polls for REVIEW.md for up to N seconds before returning. Claude Code stays in the "stopping" state, no extra API calls. Downside: the session looks frozen to the user for however long the review takes (could be minutes).

**2. Short-window opportunistic** — the Stop hook waits ~15-20 seconds (the review has a 10s initial delay already). If the review lands within that window, inject it immediately. If not, let the session end normally — the review gets picked up on the next `UserPromptSubmit` as it does today. This catches fast reviews without the polling cost.

**3. Accept the current UX** — the review already gets injected on the next prompt via `UserPromptSubmit`. The latency is "however long until the user types next," which in practice is often seconds. The only scenario where auto-prompt helps is if the user walks away.

Option 2 feels like the best balance — a short blocking wait in the Stop hook that catches most reviews without wasting API calls or freezing the session for minutes. But it's a bet on review speed.

    53→	}

   103→// handleWingmanTurnEnd handles wingman actions at turn end: triggering reviews,
   104→// auto-applying pending reviews, and showing stop notifications.
   105→func handleWingmanTurnEnd(sessionID string, totalChanges int, relModifiedFiles, relNewFiles, relDeletedFiles, allPrompts []string, commitMessage string) {
   106→	repoRoot, err := paths.RepoRoot()
   107→	if err != nil {
   108→		return
   109→	}
   110→
   111→	strat := GetStrategy()
   112→
   113→	// Trigger wingman review for auto-commit strategy (commit already happened
   114→	// in SaveStep). Manual-commit triggers wingman from the git post-commit hook
   115→	// instead, since the user commits manually.
   116→	if totalChanges > 0 && strat.Name() == strategy.StrategyNameAutoCommit && settings.IsWingmanEnabled() {
   117→		triggerWingmanReview(WingmanPayload{
   118→			SessionID:     sessionID,
   119→			RepoRoot:      repoRoot,
   120→			ModifiedFiles: relModifiedFiles,
   121→			NewFiles:      relNewFiles,
   122→			DeletedFiles:  relDeletedFiles,
   123→			Prompts:       allPrompts,
   124→			CommitMessage: commitMessage,
   125→		})
   126→	}
   127→
   128→	// Auto-apply pending wingman review on turn end
   129→	triggerWingmanAutoApplyIfPending(repoRoot)
   130→
   131→	outputWingmanStopNotification(repoRoot)
   132→}
   133→
   134→// triggerWingmanAutoApplyIfPending checks for a pending REVIEW.md and spawns
   135→// the auto-apply subprocess if conditions are met. Called from the stop hook
   136→// on every turn end (both with-changes and no-changes paths).
   137→//
   138→// When a live session exists, this is a no-op: the prompt-submit injection
   139→// will deliver the review visibly in the user's terminal instead. Background
   140→// auto-apply is only used when no sessions are alive (all ended).
   141→func triggerWingmanAutoApplyIfPending(repoRoot string) {
   142→	logCtx := logging.WithComponent(context.Background(), "wingman")
   143→	if !settings.IsWingmanEnabled() {
   144→		logging.Debug(logCtx, "wingman auto-apply skip: wingman not enabled")
   145→		return
   146→	}
   147→	if os.Getenv("ENTIRE_WINGMAN_APPLY") != "" {
   148→		logging.Debug(logCtx, "wingman auto-apply skip: already in apply subprocess")
   149→		return
   150→	}
   151→	reviewPath := filepath.Join(repoRoot, wingmanReviewFile)
   152→	if _, statErr := os.Stat(reviewPath); statErr != nil {
   153→		logging.Debug(logCtx, "wingman auto-apply skip: no REVIEW.md pending")
   154→		return
   155→	}
   156→	// Skip auto-apply if the review has no actionable issues
   157→	if !reviewHasActionableIssues(reviewPath) {
   158→		logging.Info(logCtx, "wingman auto-apply skip: review has no actionable issues, cleaning up")
   159→		_ = os.Remove(reviewPath)
   160→		return
   161→	}
   162→	wingmanState := loadWingmanStateDirect(repoRoot)
   163→	if wingmanState != nil && wingmanState.ApplyAttemptedAt != nil {
   164→		logging.Debug(logCtx, "wingman auto-apply already attempted, skipping",
   165→			slog.Time("attempted_at", *wingmanState.ApplyAttemptedAt),
   166→		)
   167→		return
   168→	}
   169→	// Don't spawn background auto-apply if a live session exists.
   170→	// The prompt-submit hook will inject REVIEW.md as additionalContext,
   171→	// which is visible to the user in their terminal.
   172→	if hasAnyLiveSession(repoRoot) {
   173→		logging.Debug(logCtx, "wingman auto-apply deferred: live session will handle via injection")
   174→		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "[wingman] Review pending — will be injected on next prompt\n")
   175→		return
   176→	}
   177→	fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "[wingman] Pending review found, spawning auto-apply (no live sessions)\n")
   178→	logging.Info(logCtx, "wingman auto-apply spawning (no live sessions)",
   179→		slog.String("review_path", reviewPath),
   180→	)
   181→	spawnDetachedWingmanApply(repoRoot)
   182→}

   184→// reviewHasActionableIssues reads a REVIEW.md and checks if it contains
   185→// actionable issue markers ([CRITICAL], [WARNING], or [SUGGESTION]).
   186→// Returns false if the file can't be read or contains no issues.
   187→func reviewHasActionableIssues(reviewPath string) bool {
   188→	data, err := os.ReadFile(reviewPath) //nolint:gosec // path is from repo-relative constant
   189→	if err != nil {
   190→		return false
   191→	}
   192→
   193→	content := string(data)
   194→
   195→	// The review format uses "### [SEVERITY] description" for each issue.
   196→	// Check for any of the severity markers in heading context.
   197→	for _, marker := range []string{"[CRITICAL]", "[WARNING]", "[SUGGESTION]"} {
   198→		if strings.Contains(content, marker) {
   199→			return true
   200→		}
   201→	}
   202→
   203→	return false
   204→}

   206→// outputWingmanStopNotification outputs a systemMessage notification about
   207→// wingman status at the end of a stop hook. This makes wingman activity visible
   208→// in the agent terminal without injecting context into the agent's conversation.
   209→// Best-effort: status may be stale due to concurrent wingman processes.
   210→func outputWingmanStopNotification(repoRoot string) {

   212→		return
   213→	}
   214→	if os.Getenv("ENTIRE_WINGMAN_APPLY") != "" {
   215→		return
   216→	}

   218→	lockPath := filepath.Join(repoRoot, wingmanLockFile)
   219→	if info, err := os.Stat(lockPath); err == nil && time.Since(info.ModTime()) <= wingmanNotificationLockThreshold {
   220→		_ = outputHookMessage("[Wingman] Reviewing your changes...") //nolint:errcheck // best-effort notification
   221→		return
   222→	}
   223→
   224→	reviewPath := filepath.Join(repoRoot, wingmanReviewFile)
   225→	if _, err := os.Stat(reviewPath); err == nil && reviewHasActionableIssues(reviewPath) {
   226→		_ = outputHookMessage("[Wingman] Review pending \u2014 will be addressed on your next prompt") //nolint:errcheck // best-effort notification
   227→		return
   228→	}
   229→}

   207→// computeDiff gets the full branch diff for review. It diffs the current HEAD
   208→// against the merge base with the default branch (main/master), giving the
   209→// reviewer a holistic view of all branch changes rather than just one commit.
   210→func computeDiff(repoRoot string) (string, error) {
   211→	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), wingmanGitTimeout)
   212→	defer cancel()
   213→
   214→	// Find the merge base with the default branch for a holistic branch diff.
   215→	mergeBase := findMergeBase(ctx, repoRoot)
   216→	if mergeBase != "" {
   217→		wingmanLog("using merge-base %s for branch diff", mergeBase)
   218→		diff, err := gitDiff(ctx, repoRoot, mergeBase)
   219→		if err == nil && strings.TrimSpace(diff) != "" {
   220→			return diff, nil
   221→		}
   222→		// Fall through to HEAD diff if merge-base diff fails or is empty
   223→	}
   224→
   225→	// Fallback: diff uncommitted changes against HEAD
   226→	wingmanLog("falling back to HEAD diff")
   227→	diff, err := gitDiff(ctx, repoRoot, "HEAD")
   228→	if err != nil {
   229→		return "", fmt.Errorf("git diff failed: %w", err)
   230→	}
   231→
   232→	// If no uncommitted changes, try the latest commit itself
   233→	if strings.TrimSpace(diff) == "" {
   234→		diff, err = gitDiff(ctx, repoRoot, "HEAD~1", "HEAD")
   235→		if err != nil {
   236→			return "", fmt.Errorf("git diff for latest commit failed: %w", err)
   237→		}
   238→	}
   239→
   240→	return diff, nil
   241→}

   243→// findMergeBase returns the merge-base commit between HEAD and the default
   244→// branch (tries main, then master). Returns empty string if not found.
   245→func findMergeBase(ctx context.Context, repoRoot string) string {
   246→	for _, branch := range []string{"main", "master"} {
   247→		cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "git", "merge-base", branch, "HEAD") //nolint:gosec // branch is from hardcoded slice
   248→		cmd.Dir = repoRoot
   249→		out, err := cmd.Output()
   250→		if err == nil {
   251→			return strings.TrimSpace(string(out))
   252→		}
   253→	}
   254→	return ""
   255→}

   257→// gitDiff runs git diff with the given args and returns stdout.
   258→func gitDiff(ctx context.Context, repoRoot string, args ...string) (string, error) {
   259→	fullArgs := append([]string{"diff"}, args...)
   260→	cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "git", fullArgs...) //nolint:gosec // args are from internal logic
   261→	cmd.Dir = repoRoot
   262→	var stdout, stderr bytes.Buffer
   263→	cmd.Stdout = &stdout
   264→	cmd.Stderr = &stderr
   265→	if err := cmd.Run(); err != nil {
   266→		return "", fmt.Errorf("git diff %v: %w (stderr: %s)", args, err, stderr.String())
   267→	}
   268→	return stdout.String(), nil
   269→}

   348→// staleActiveSessionThreshold is the maximum age of a session state file in an
   349→// ACTIVE phase before it is considered stale (crashed agent) and ignored by
   350→// hasAnyLiveSession. Only applies to ACTIVE/ACTIVE_COMMITTED phases — an IDLE
   351→// session is always considered live regardless of age (user may just be away).
   352→const staleActiveSessionThreshold = 4 * time.Hour

   354→// hasAnyLiveSession checks if any session is in a non-ENDED phase (IDLE,
   355→// ACTIVE, or ACTIVE_COMMITTED). Used to decide whether to defer review
   356→// application to the prompt-submit injection (visible to user) vs background
   357→// auto-apply (invisible).
   358→//
   359→// ACTIVE/ACTIVE_COMMITTED sessions older than staleActiveSessionThreshold are
   360→// skipped as likely orphaned from crashed processes. IDLE sessions are always
   361→// considered live regardless of age.
   362→func hasAnyLiveSession(repoRoot string) bool {
   363→	sessDir := findSessionStateDir(repoRoot)
   364→	if sessDir == "" {
   365→		return false
   366→	}
   367→
   368→	entries, err := os.ReadDir(sessDir)
   369→	if err != nil {
   370→		return false
   371→	}
   372→
   373→	const maxCheck = 50
   374→	checked := 0
   375→	for _, entry := range entries {
   376→		if checked >= maxCheck {
   377→			wingmanLog("stopping live-session scan after %d entries; assuming live session may exist", checked)
   378→			return true
   379→		}
   380→		name := entry.Name()
   381→		if !strings.HasSuffix(name, ".json") {
   382→			continue
   383→		}
   384→		checked++
   385→
   386→		sid := strings.TrimSuffix(name, ".json")
   387→		info := readSessionPhaseInfo(sessDir, sid)
   388→		if info.Phase == "" || info.Phase == string(session.PhaseEnded) {
   389→			continue
   390→		}
   391→
   392→		// ACTIVE/ACTIVE_COMMITTED sessions that haven't had a real agent
   393→		// interaction in a long time are likely orphaned from crashed agents.
   394→		// Uses LastInteractionTime from JSON (not file modtime) because
   395→		// PostCommit saves all session files on every commit, refreshing
   396→		// modtime even for stale sessions.
   397→		// IDLE sessions are always considered live (user may just be away).
   398→		if session.PhaseFromString(info.Phase).IsActive() {
   399→			if info.LastInteractionTime != nil && time.Since(*info.LastInteractionTime) > staleActiveSessionThreshold {
   400→				wingmanLog("skipping stale active session %s (phase=%s, last_interaction=%s ago)", sid, info.Phase, time.Since(*info.LastInteractionTime).Round(time.Second))
   401→				continue
   402→			}
   403→		}
   404→
   405→		wingmanLog("found live session %s (phase=%s)", sid, info.Phase)
   406→		return true
   407→	}
   408→
   409→	return false
   410→}

   412→// findSessionStateDir locates the .git/entire-sessions/ directory by
   413→// reading .git to handle both normal repos and worktrees.
   414→func findSessionStateDir(repoRoot string) string {
   415→	gitPath := filepath.Join(repoRoot, ".git")
   416→	info, err := os.Stat(gitPath)
   417→	if err != nil {
   418→		return ""
   419→	}
   420→
   421→	var gitDir string
   422→	if info.IsDir() {
   423→		// Normal repo: .git is a directory
   424→		gitDir = gitPath
   425→	} else {
   426→		// Worktree: .git is a file containing "gitdir: <path>"
   427→		data, readErr := os.ReadFile(gitPath) //nolint:gosec // path from repoRoot
   428→		if readErr != nil {
   429→			return ""
   430→		}
   431→		content := strings.TrimSpace(string(data))
   432→		if !strings.HasPrefix(content, "gitdir: ") {
   433→			return ""
   434→		}
   435→		gitDir = strings.TrimPrefix(content, "gitdir: ")
   436→		if !filepath.IsAbs(gitDir) {
   437→			gitDir = filepath.Join(repoRoot, gitDir)
   438→		}
   439→		// For worktrees, session state is in the common dir
   440→		// .git/worktrees/<name> → ../../ is the common .git dir
   441→		commonDir := filepath.Join(gitDir, "..", "..")
   442→		gitDir = filepath.Clean(commonDir)
   443→	}
   444→
   445→	sessDir := filepath.Join(gitDir, "entire-sessions")
   446→	if _, statErr := os.Stat(sessDir); statErr != nil {
   447→		return ""
   448→	}
   449→	return sessDir
   450→}

   492→	case state == nil:
   493→		wingmanLog("no wingman state found, proceeding without session check")
   494→	case state.ApplyAttemptedAt != nil:
   495→		wingmanLog("apply already attempted at %s, skipping", state.ApplyAttemptedAt.Format(time.RFC3339))
   496→		return nil
   497→	default:
   498→		wingmanLog("wingman state loaded: session=%s", state.SessionID)
   499→	}
   500→
   501→	// Re-check session hasn't become active (user may have typed during spawn delay).
   502→	// IDLE and ENDED are safe — only ACTIVE/ACTIVE_COMMITTED should block.
   503→	if state != nil && state.SessionID != "" {
   504→		sessDir := findSessionStateDir(repoRoot)
   505→		if sessDir != "" {
   506→			phaseInfo := readSessionPhaseInfo(sessDir, state.SessionID)
   507→			if phaseInfo.Phase != "" && session.PhaseFromString(phaseInfo.Phase).IsActive() {
   508→				wingmanLog("session is active (phase=%s), aborting (next stop hook will retry)", phaseInfo.Phase)
   509→				return nil
   510→			}
   511→			wingmanLog("session phase=%s, safe to proceed", phaseInfo.Phase)
   512→		}
   513→	}
   514→
   515→	// Mark apply as attempted BEFORE triggering
   516→	if state != nil {
   517→		now := time.Now()
   518→		state.ApplyAttemptedAt = &now
   519→		saveWingmanStateDirect(repoRoot, state)
   520→	}
   521→
   522→	wingmanLog("triggering auto-apply via claude --continue")
   523→	applyStart := time.Now()
   524→	if err := triggerAutoApply(repoRoot); err != nil {
   525→		wingmanLog("ERROR auto-apply failed after %s: %v", time.Since(applyStart).Round(time.Millisecond), err)
   526→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to trigger auto-apply: %w", err)
   527→	}
   528→	wingmanLog("auto-apply completed in %s", time.Since(applyStart).Round(time.Millisecond))
   529→
   530→	return nil
   531→}
   532→
   533→// triggerAutoApply spawns claude --continue to apply the review suggestions.
   534→// NOTE: This uses --continue which is Claude-specific and not part of the
   535→// Prompter interface. If the wingman agent is not claude-code, auto-apply
   536→// is skipped.
   537→func triggerAutoApply(repoRoot string) error {
   538→	agentName := resolveWingmanAgent()
   539→	if agentName != agent.AgentNameClaudeCode {
   540→		wingmanLog("auto-apply skipped: --continue is only supported for claude-code (agent=%s)", agentName)
   541→		return nil
   542→	}
   543→
   544→	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), wingmanApplyTimeout)
   545→	defer cancel()
   546→
   547→	cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "claude",
   548→		"--continue",
   549→		"--print",
   550→		"--setting-sources", "",
   551→		// Auto-accept edits so the agent can modify files and delete REVIEW.md
   552→		// without requiring user consent (this runs in a background process).
   553→		"--permission-mode", "acceptEdits",
   554→		wingmanApplyInstruction,
   555→	)
   556→	cmd.Dir = repoRoot
   557→	// Strip GIT_* env vars to prevent hook interference, and set
   558→	// ENTIRE_WINGMAN_APPLY=1 so git hooks (post-commit) know not to
   559→	// trigger another wingman review (prevents infinite recursion).
   560→	env := agent.StripGitEnv(os.Environ())
   561→	env = append(env, "ENTIRE_WINGMAN_APPLY=1")
   562→	cmd.Env = env
   563→
   564→	var stdout, stderr bytes.Buffer
   565→	cmd.Stdout = &stdout
   566→	cmd.Stderr = &stderr
   567→
   568→	return cmd.Run() //nolint:wrapcheck // caller wraps
   569→}
   570→
   571→// saveWingmanStateDirect writes the wingman state file directly to a known path
   572→// under repoRoot, avoiding os.Chdir (which mutates process-wide state).
   573→func saveWingmanStateDirect(repoRoot string, state *WingmanState) {
   574→	statePath := filepath.Join(repoRoot, wingmanStateFile)
   575→	if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(statePath), 0o750); err != nil {
   576→		return
   577→	}
   578→	data, err := json.MarshalIndent(state, "", "  ")
   579→	if err != nil {
   580→		return
   581→	}
   582→	//nolint:gosec,errcheck // G306: state file is config, not secrets; best-effort write
   583→	_ = os.WriteFile(statePath, data, 0o644)
   584→}

   672→func (s *GeminiSession) CreateGeminiTranscript(prompt string, changes []FileChange) string {

   674→	messages := []map[string]interface{}{

   678→		},

   681→			"content": "I'll help you with that.",

   683→	}
   684→
   685→	for _, change := range changes {
   686→		messages = append(messages, map[string]interface{}{

   689→			"input": map[string]string{

   691→				"content": change.Content,

   694→		messages = append(messages, map[string]interface{}{

   700→	messages = append(messages, map[string]interface{}{

   702→		"content": "Done!",
   703→	})

   705→	transcript := map[string]interface{}{

1→// wingman_lifecycle.go contains wingman integration hooks for the lifecycle dispatcher.
     2→// These functions are called from lifecycle.go event handlers to inject wingman
     3→// review state into session start banners, turn start context, and turn end actions.
     4→package cli
     5→
     6→import (
     7→	"context"
     8→	"fmt"
     9→	"log/slog"
    10→	"os"
    11→	"path/filepath"
    12→	"strings"
    13→	"time"
    14→
    15→	"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/logging"
    16→	"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/paths"
    17→	"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/settings"
    18→	"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/strategy"
    19→)
    20→
    21→// wingmanNotificationLockThreshold is the maximum lock file age for showing
    22→// "Reviewing your changes..." notifications. Much tighter than staleLockThreshold
    23→// (used for lock acquisition) because a real review takes at most
    24→// wingmanInitialDelay (10s) + wingmanReviewTimeout (5m) ≈ 6 minutes.
    25→// A lock older than this is almost certainly stale for notification purposes.
    26→const wingmanNotificationLockThreshold = 10 * time.Minute
    27→
    28→// appendWingmanSessionStartStatus appends wingman status to the session start banner.
    29→// Returns the message with wingman status appended.
    30→func appendWingmanSessionStartStatus(message string) string {
    31→	if !settings.IsWingmanEnabled() {
    32→		return message
    33→	}
    34→
    35→	repoRoot, rootErr := paths.RepoRoot()
    36→	if rootErr != nil {
    37→		return message + "\n  Wingman is active: your changes will be automatically reviewed."
    38→	}
    39→
    40→	reviewPath := filepath.Join(repoRoot, wingmanReviewFile)
    41→	if _, statErr := os.Stat(reviewPath); statErr == nil && reviewHasActionableIssues(reviewPath) {
    42→		return message + "\n  Wingman: a review is pending and will be addressed on your next prompt."
    43→	}
    44→	return message + "\n  Wingman is active: your changes will be automatically reviewed."
    45→}
    46→
    47→// handleWingmanTurnStart checks for a pending wingman review and injects it
    48→// as additionalContext so the agent addresses it before the user's request.
    49→// Returns true if a hook response was written to stdout (caller should return early).
    50→func handleWingmanTurnStart(sessionID string) bool {
    51→	if !settings.IsWingmanEnabled() {
    52→		return false
    53→	}
    54→
    55→	repoRoot, rootErr := paths.RepoRoot()
    56→	if rootErr != nil {
    57→		return false
    58→	}
    59→
    60→	wingmanLogCtx := logging.WithComponent(context.Background(), "wingman")
    61→
    62→	// If a review is pending, check if it has actionable issues before injecting
    63→	reviewPath := filepath.Join(repoRoot, wingmanReviewFile)
    64→	if _, statErr := os.Stat(reviewPath); statErr == nil {
    65→		if !reviewHasActionableIssues(reviewPath) {
    66→			// No actionable issues — clean up and notify the user
    67→			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "[wingman] Review has no actionable issues, cleaning up\n")
    68→			logging.Info(wingmanLogCtx, "wingman review has no actionable issues, skipping injection",
    69→				slog.String("session_id", sessionID),
    70→			)
    71→			_ = os.Remove(reviewPath)
    72→			_ = outputHookMessage("[Wingman] Reviewed your changes — no issues found.") //nolint:errcheck // best-effort notification
    73→		} else {
    74→			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "[wingman] Review available: .entire/REVIEW.md — injecting into context\n")
    75→			logging.Info(wingmanLogCtx, "wingman injecting review instruction on prompt-submit",
    76→				slog.String("session_id", sessionID),
    77→			)
    78→			if err := outputHookResponseWithContextAndMessage(
    79→				wingmanApplyInstruction,
    80→				"[Wingman] A code review is pending and will be addressed before your request.",
    81→			); err != nil {
    82→				fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "[wingman] Warning: failed to inject review instruction: %v\n", err)
    83→			} else {
    84→				return true // Hook response written to stdout — caller must return
    85→			}
    86→		}
    87→	}
    88→
    89→	// Notify if a review is currently in progress (fresh lock file).
    90→	lockPath := filepath.Join(repoRoot, wingmanLockFile)
    91→	if lockInfo, statErr := os.Stat(lockPath); statErr == nil && time.Since(lockInfo.ModTime()) <= wingmanNotificationLockThreshold {
    92→		logging.Info(wingmanLogCtx, "wingman review in progress",
    93→			slog.String("session_id", sessionID),
    94→		)
    95→		if err := outputHookMessage("[Wingman] Review in progress..."); err != nil {
    96→			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "[wingman] Warning: failed to output review-in-progress message: %v\n", err)
    97→		}
    98→	}
    99→
   100→	return false
   101→}
   102→
   103→// handleWingmanTurnEnd handles wingman actions at turn end: triggering reviews,
   104→// auto-applying pending reviews, and showing stop notifications.
   105→func handleWingmanTurnEnd(sessionID string, totalChanges int, relModifiedFiles, relNewFiles, relDeletedFiles, allPrompts []string, commitMessage string) {
   106→	repoRoot, err := paths.RepoRoot()
   107→	if err != nil {
   108→		return
   109→	}
   110→
   111→	strat := GetStrategy()
   112→
   113→	// Trigger wingman review for auto-commit strategy (commit already happened
   114→	// in SaveStep). Manual-commit triggers wingman from the git post-commit hook
   115→	// instead, since the user commits manually.
   116→	if totalChanges > 0 && strat.Name() == strategy.StrategyNameAutoCommit && settings.IsWingmanEnabled() {
   117→		triggerWingmanReview(WingmanPayload{
   118→			SessionID:     sessionID,
   119→			RepoRoot:      repoRoot,
   120→			ModifiedFiles: relModifiedFiles,
   121→			NewFiles:      relNewFiles,
   122→			DeletedFiles:  relDeletedFiles,
   123→			Prompts:       allPrompts,
   124→			CommitMessage: commitMessage,
   125→		})
   126→	}
   127→
   128→	// Auto-apply pending wingman review on turn end
   129→	triggerWingmanAutoApplyIfPending(repoRoot)
   130→
   131→	outputWingmanStopNotification(repoRoot)
   132→}
   133→
   134→// triggerWingmanAutoApplyIfPending checks for a pending REVIEW.md and spawns
   135→// the auto-apply subprocess if conditions are met. Called from the stop hook
   136→// on every turn end (both with-changes and no-changes paths).
   137→//
   138→// When a live session exists, this is a no-op: the prompt-submit injection
   139→// will deliver the review visibly in the user's terminal instead. Background
   140→// auto-apply is only used when no sessions are alive (all ended).
   141→func triggerWingmanAutoApplyIfPending(repoRoot string) {
   142→	logCtx := logging.WithComponent(context.Background(), "wingman")
   143→	if !settings.IsWingmanEnabled() {
   144→		logging.Debug(logCtx, "wingman auto-apply skip: wingman not enabled")
   145→		return
   146→	}
   147→	if os.Getenv("ENTIRE_WINGMAN_APPLY") != "" {
   148→		logging.Debug(logCtx, "wingman auto-apply skip: already in apply subprocess")
   149→		return
   150→	}
   151→	reviewPath := filepath.Join(repoRoot, wingmanReviewFile)
   152→	if _, statErr := os.Stat(reviewPath); statErr != nil {
   153→		logging.Debug(logCtx, "wingman auto-apply skip: no REVIEW.md pending")
   154→		return
   155→	}
   156→	// Skip auto-apply if the review has no actionable issues
   157→	if !reviewHasActionableIssues(reviewPath) {
   158→		logging.Info(logCtx, "wingman auto-apply skip: review has no actionable issues, cleaning up")
   159→		_ = os.Remove(reviewPath)
   160→		return
   161→	}
   162→	wingmanState := loadWingmanStateDirect(repoRoot)
   163→	if wingmanState != nil && wingmanState.ApplyAttemptedAt != nil {
   164→		logging.Debug(logCtx, "wingman auto-apply already attempted, skipping",
   165→			slog.Time("attempted_at", *wingmanState.ApplyAttemptedAt),
   166→		)
   167→		return
   168→	}
   169→	// Don't spawn background auto-apply if a live session exists.
   170→	// The prompt-submit hook will inject REVIEW.md as additionalContext,
   171→	// which is visible to the user in their terminal.
   172→	if hasAnyLiveSession(repoRoot) {
   173→		logging.Debug(logCtx, "wingman auto-apply deferred: live session will handle via injection")
   174→		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "[wingman] Review pending — will be injected on next prompt\n")
   175→		return
   176→	}
   177→	fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "[wingman] Pending review found, spawning auto-apply (no live sessions)\n")
   178→	logging.Info(logCtx, "wingman auto-apply spawning (no live sessions)",
   179→		slog.String("review_path", reviewPath),
   180→	)
   181→	spawnDetachedWingmanApply(repoRoot)
   182→}
   183→
   184→// reviewHasActionableIssues reads a REVIEW.md and checks if it contains
   185→// actionable issue markers ([CRITICAL], [WARNING], or [SUGGESTION]).
   186→// Returns false if the file can't be read or contains no issues.
   187→func reviewHasActionableIssues(reviewPath string) bool {
   188→	data, err := os.ReadFile(reviewPath) //nolint:gosec // path is from repo-relative constant
   189→	if err != nil {
   190→		return false
   191→	}
   192→
   193→	content := string(data)
   194→
   195→	// The review format uses "### [SEVERITY] description" for each issue.
   196→	// Check for any of the severity markers in heading context.
   197→	for _, marker := range []string{"[CRITICAL]", "[WARNING]", "[SUGGESTION]"} {
   198→		if strings.Contains(content, marker) {
   199→			return true
   200→		}
   201→	}
   202→
   203→	return false
   204→}
   205→
   206→// outputWingmanStopNotification outputs a systemMessage notification about
   207→// wingman status at the end of a stop hook. This makes wingman activity visible
   208→// in the agent terminal without injecting context into the agent's conversation.
   209→// Best-effort: status may be stale due to concurrent wingman processes.
   210→func outputWingmanStopNotification(repoRoot string) {
   211→	if !settings.IsWingmanEnabled() {
   212→		return
   213→	}
   214→	if os.Getenv("ENTIRE_WINGMAN_APPLY") != "" {
   215→		return
   216→	}
   217→
   218→	lockPath := filepath.Join(repoRoot, wingmanLockFile)
   219→	if info, err := os.Stat(lockPath); err == nil && time.Since(info.ModTime()) <= wingmanNotificationLockThreshold {
   220→		_ = outputHookMessage("[Wingman] Reviewing your changes...") //nolint:errcheck // best-effort notification
   221→		return
   222→	}
   223→
   224→	reviewPath := filepath.Join(repoRoot, wingmanReviewFile)
   225→	if _, err := os.Stat(reviewPath); err == nil && reviewHasActionableIssues(reviewPath) {
   226→		_ = outputHookMessage("[Wingman] Review pending \u2014 will be addressed on your next prompt") //nolint:errcheck // best-effort notification
   227→		return
   228→	}
   229→}
   230→

1→# Entire CLI Hooks for Claude Code
     2→
     3→This document describes the hooks that Entire installs in Claude Code's `.claude/settings.json` to track AI-assisted development sessions.
     4→
     5→## Overview
     6→
     7→Entire integrates with Claude Code through six hooks that fire at different points during a session:
     8→
     9→| Hook                     | Trigger                        | Purpose                                        |
    10→| ------------------------ | ------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------- |
    11→| `SessionStart`           | New chat session begins        | Generate and persist Entire session ID         |
    12→| `UserPromptSubmit`       | User submits a prompt          | Capture pre-prompt state, check for conflicts  |
    13→| `Stop`                   | Claude finishes responding     | Create checkpoint with code + metadata         |
    14→| `PreToolUse[Task]`       | Subagent is about to start     | Capture pre-task state for diff computation    |
    15→| `PostToolUse[Task]`      | Subagent finishes              | Create final checkpoint for subagent work      |
    16→| `PostToolUse[TodoWrite]` | Subagent updates its todo list | Create incremental checkpoint if files changed |
    17→
    18→### Critical Capabilities
    19→
    20→  1. Prompt blocking - UserPromptSubmit hook needs to support returning a response to be shown in the cli session.
    21→    - Claude Code allows us to return a JSON response to stdout that can:
    22→      - Allow continuation: {"continue": true}
    23→      - Block with message: {"continue": false, "stopReason": "Your message here"}
    24→  2. Transcript access - Hooks receive transcript path; system needs to read it for:
    25→    - Extracting user prompts
    26→    - Extracting modified files
    27→    - Generating summaries
    28→  3. Tool use ID tracking - For subagent checkpoints, need unique tool_use_id to correlate PreToolUse and PostToolUse events
    29→  4. Stdin parsing - Hook input comes as JSON on stdin; agent must define its input schema
    30→
    31→## Detailed Hook Info
    32→
    33→### `SessionStart`
    34→
    35→- **Command**: `entire hooks claude-code session-start`
    36→- **Handler**: `handleSessionStart()` in `hooks_claudecode_handlers.go:907`
    37→
    38→Fires when a new chat session begins in Claude Code.
    39→
    40→**What it does:**
    41→
    42→1.  **Parse Input**: Reads session details from Claude Code's hook payload (`session_id`, `session_ref`).
    43→2.  **Generate Entire Session ID**: Creates a date-prefixed identifier by combining today's date with the model's session ID (e.g., `2026-01-15-ab310c99-f579-4a12-8b3c-1234567890ab`).
    44→3.  **Persist Session ID**: Writes the Entire session ID to `.entire/current_session`. This file is read by subsequent hooks to maintain session context across hook invocations, even if the session spans midnight (date boundary).
    45→
    46→### `UserPromptSubmit`
    47→
    48→- **Command**: `entire hooks claude-code user-prompt-submit`
    49→- **Handler**: `captureInitialState()` in `hooks_claudecode_handlers.go:248`
    50→
    51→Fires every time the user submits a prompt. Prepares the repository state tracking _before_ Claude makes any changes.
    52→
    53→**What it does:**
    54→
    55→1.  **Concurrent Session Check**:
    56→
    57→    - Queries the strategy to check if another Entire session has uncommitted checkpoints on the same HEAD commit.
    58→    - If a conflict is found, outputs a JSON response that blocks the prompt and shows a warning to the user.
    59→    - The warning includes the other session's initial prompt (if available) and a resume command.
    60→    - Sets `ConcurrentWarningShown` flag in session state so the user can continue on the next prompt.
    61→    - Once the user commits their changes (or the conflict resolves), the flag is cleared automatically.
    62→
    63→2.  **Capture Pre-Prompt State**:
    64→
    65→    - Runs `git status` to get a list of all **untracked files** in the repository.
    66→    - Saves this list to `.entire/tmp/pre-prompt-<session-id>.json`.
    67→    - This baseline is compared later (in the `Stop` hook) to determine which files were newly created by Claude.
    68→    - Records the current transcript line count (`StepTranscriptStart`) for incremental token usage calculation.
    69→
    70→3.  **Initialize Session Strategy**:
    71→    - For strategies that implement `SessionInitializer`, calls `InitializeSession()`.
    72→    - **Manual-commit strategy**: Creates or validates the shadow branch (`entire/<HEAD-hash[:7]>`), saves session state to `.git/entire-sessions/<session-id>.json` with `BaseCommit`, `WorktreePath`, and `AgentType`.
    73→    - Handles shadow branch conflicts (from other worktrees) and session ID conflicts with appropriate error messages and recovery options.
    74→
    75→### `Stop`
    76→
    77→- **Command**: `entire hooks claude-code stop`
    78→- **Handler**: `commitWithMetadata()` in `hooks_claudecode_handlers.go:288`
    79→
    80→Fires when Claude finishes responding. Does **not** fire on user interrupt (Ctrl+C).
    81→
    82→**What it does:**
    83→
    84→1.  **Parse Transcript**:
    85→
    86→    - Reads the JSONL transcript from the path provided by Claude Code.
    87→    - Parses the full transcript. `CheckpointTranscriptStart` (or `StepTranscriptStart` from pre-prompt state) is used to detect whether new content exists since the last checkpoint.
    88→    - Extracts **modified files** by scanning for Write/Edit tool uses in the transcript.
    89→
    90→2.  **Extract and Save Metadata** (to `.entire/metadata/<session-id>/`):
    91→
    92→    - `full.jsonl` - Copy of the complete transcript.
    93→    - `prompt.txt` - All user prompts from this interaction, separated by `---`.
    94→    - `summary.txt` - The last assistant message (used as checkpoint summary).
    95→    - `context.md` - Generated context file with commit message, session info, and file lists.
    96→
    97→3.  **Compute File Changes**:
    98→
    99→    - **Modified files**: Extracted from transcript (Write/Edit tool invocations).
   100→    - **New files**: Compare current untracked files against pre-prompt state to find files created by Claude.
   101→    - **Deleted files**: Query `git status` for tracked files that no longer exist.
   102→    - All paths are normalized relative to repo root (not cwd) to handle Claude running from subdirectories.
   103→
   104→4.  **Generate Commit Message**: Derives from the last user prompt, truncated and formatted appropriately.
   105→
   106→5.  **Calculate Token Usage**:
   107→
   108→    - Parses the transcript from `StepTranscriptStart` (captured at prompt start) to calculate tokens used in this turn.
   109→    - Extracts token counts from assistant messages: input tokens, cache creation/read tokens, output tokens.
   110→    - Deduplicates by message ID (streaming creates multiple rows per message; uses highest output_tokens).
   111→    - Finds spawned subagents by scanning for `agentId:` in Task tool results.
   112→    - Calculates subagent token usage from their transcript files (`agent-<id>.jsonl`).
   113→    - Aggregates into a `TokenUsage` struct with nested `SubagentTokens`.
   114→
   115→6.  **Invoke Strategy**:
   116→
   117→    - Builds a `SaveContext` with session ID, file lists, metadata paths, git author info, and token usage.
   118→    - Calls `strategy.SaveChanges(ctx)` to create the checkpoint.
   119→    - **Manual-commit**: Builds a git tree in-memory and commits to the shadow branch.
   120→    - **Auto-commit**: Creates a commit on the active branch with the `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer.
   121→    - Token usage is stored in `metadata.json` for later analysis and reporting.
   122→
   123→7.  **Update Session State**: Updates `CheckpointTranscriptStart` to track transcript position for detecting new content in future checkpoints (auto-commit strategy only).
   124→
   125→8.  **Cleanup**: Deletes the temporary `.entire/tmp/pre-prompt-<session-id>.json` file.
   126→
   127→### `PreToolUse[Task]`
   128→
   129→- **Command**: `entire hooks claude-code pre-task`
   130→- **Handler**: `handlePreTask()` in `hooks_claudecode_handlers.go:668`
   131→
   132→Fires just before a subagent (Task tool) begins execution. Captures the current state so that file changes can be computed when the task completes.
   133→
   134→**What it does:**
   135→
   136→1.  **Parse Input**: Extracts `tool_use_id`, `session_id`, `transcript_path`, and `tool_input` from the hook payload.
   137→
   138→2.  **Extract Subagent Info**: Parses `tool_input` to get:
   139→
   140→    - `subagent_type` - The type of subagent (e.g., "Explore", "reviewer", "dev").
   141→    - `description` - The task description (e.g., "Find authentication files").
   142→
   143→3.  **Capture Pre-Task State**:
   144→
   145→    - Runs `git status` to get current untracked files.
   146→    - Saves to `.entire/tmp/pre-task-<tool-use-id>.json`.
   147→    - This baseline is used by `PostToolUse[Task]` to determine which files the subagent created.
   148→    - **Note**: No checkpoint/commit is created at this stage. Commits are only created during task completion (`PostToolUse[Task]` or `PostToolUse[TodoWrite]`) and only if there are actual file changes.
   149→
   150→### `PostToolUse[Task]`
   151→
   152→- **Command**: `entire hooks claude-code post-task`
   153→- **Handler**: `handlePostTask()` in `hooks_claudecode_handlers.go:770`
   154→
   155→Fires after a subagent finishes its work. Creates the final checkpoint for the subagent's task.
   156→
   157→**What it does:**
   158→
   159→1.  **Parse Input**: Extracts `tool_use_id`, `agent_id` (from `tool_response.agentId`), `session_id`, `transcript_path`, and `tool_input`.
   160→
   161→2.  **Locate Subagent Transcript**:
   162→
   163→    - Constructs path: `<transcript_dir>/agent-<agent_id>.jsonl`.
   164→    - If the subagent transcript exists, uses it for file extraction; otherwise falls back to main transcript.
   165→
   166→3.  **Extract Modified Files**: Parses the transcript (subagent or main) to find Write/Edit tool invocations.
   167→
   168→4.  **Compute New Files**:
   169→
   170→    - Loads pre-task state from `.entire/tmp/pre-task-<tool-use-id>.json`.
   171→    - Compares current untracked files against the pre-task snapshot.
   172→    - Files that are now untracked but weren't before = files created by the subagent.
   173→
   174→5.  **Find Checkpoint UUID**: Scans the main transcript for any checkpoint UUID associated with this `tool_use_id` (used for rewind linking).
   175→
   176→6.  **Save Final Checkpoint**:
   177→
   178→    - Builds `TaskCheckpointContext` with all file changes, transcript paths, subagent info, and checkpoint UUID.
   179→    - Calls `strategy.SaveTaskCheckpoint(ctx)`.
   180→    - Creates a commit with the subagent's file changes and metadata including the subagent transcript.
   181→
   182→7.  **Cleanup**: Deletes `.entire/tmp/pre-task-<tool-use-id>.json`.
   183→
   184→### `PostToolUse[TodoWrite]`
   185→
   186→- **Command**: `entire hooks claude-code post-todo`
   187→- **Handler**: `handlePostTodo()` in `hooks_claudecode_handlers.go:550`
   188→
   189→Fires whenever a subagent updates its todo list. Enables fine-grained, incremental checkpointing _during_ subagent execution.
   190→
   191→**What it does:**
   192→
   193→1.  **Subagent Context Check**:
   194→
   195→    - Looks for an active pre-task file (`.entire/tmp/pre-task-*.json`).
   196→    - If no pre-task file exists, this is a main agent `TodoWrite` - skip silently.
   197→    - This ensures incremental checkpoints only happen inside subagent Task tool invocations.
   198→
   199→2.  **Detect File Changes**:
   200→
   201→    - Calls `DetectFileChanges()` to check for modifications since the last checkpoint.
   202→    - Compares against git worktree status for modified, new, and deleted files.
   203→
   204→3.  **Skip if No Changes**: If no files have changed, logs a message and returns without creating a checkpoint.
   205→
   206→4.  **Extract Todo Content**:
   207→
   208→    - Parses the `tool_input.todos` array from the hook payload.
   209→    - Looks for the **last completed** todo item - this represents the work just finished.
   210→    - If no completed items (first TodoWrite), uses "Planning: N todos" format.
   211→    - This becomes the checkpoint description (e.g., "Completed: Add user authentication endpoint").
   212→
   213→5.  **Get Checkpoint Sequence**: Calls `GetNextCheckpointSequence()` to get an incrementing number for this task.
   214→
   215→6.  **Save Incremental Checkpoint**:
   216→    - Builds `TaskCheckpointContext` with `IsIncremental: true`, sequence number, and todo content.
   217→    - Calls `strategy.SaveTaskCheckpoint(ctx)`.
   218→    - Creates a small commit capturing the incremental progress.
   219→
   220→**Example sequence during a subagent Task:**
   221→
   222→```
   223→PreToolUse[Task]       → (no checkpoint - only captures pre-task state)
   224→PostToolUse[TodoWrite] → Checkpoint #1: "Planning: 5 todos" (if files changed)
   225→PostToolUse[TodoWrite] → Checkpoint #2: "Completed: Create user model"
   226→PostToolUse[TodoWrite] → Checkpoint #3: "Completed: Add login endpoint"
   227→PostToolUse[Task]      → Checkpoint #4: Final checkpoint with all changes
   228→```
   229→

1→// wingman_lifecycle.go contains wingman integration hooks for the lifecycle dispatcher.
     2→// These functions are called from lifecycle.go event handlers to inject wingman
     3→// review state into session start banners, turn start context, and turn end actions.
     4→package cli
     5→
     6→import (
     7→	"context"
     8→	"fmt"
     9→	"log/slog"
    10→	"os"
    11→	"path/filepath"
    12→	"strings"
    13→	"time"
    14→
    15→	"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/logging"
    16→	"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/paths"
    17→	"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/settings"
    18→	"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/strategy"
    19→)
    20→
    21→// wingmanNotificationLockThreshold is the maximum lock file age for showing
    22→// "Reviewing your changes..." notifications. Much tighter than staleLockThreshold
    23→// (used for lock acquisition) because a real review takes at most
    24→// wingmanInitialDelay (10s) + wingmanReviewTimeout (5m) ≈ 6 minutes.
    25→// A lock older than this is almost certainly stale for notification purposes.
    26→const wingmanNotificationLockThreshold = 10 * time.Minute
    27→
    28→// appendWingmanSessionStartStatus appends wingman status to the session start banner.
    29→// Returns the message with wingman status appended.
    30→func appendWingmanSessionStartStatus(message string) string {
    31→	if !settings.IsWingmanEnabled() {
    32→		return message
    33→	}
    34→
    35→	repoRoot, rootErr := paths.RepoRoot()
    36→	if rootErr != nil {
    37→		return message + "\n  Wingman is active: your changes will be automatically reviewed."
    38→	}
    39→
    40→	reviewPath := filepath.Join(repoRoot, wingmanReviewFile)
    41→	if _, statErr := os.Stat(reviewPath); statErr == nil && reviewHasActionableIssues(reviewPath) {
    42→		return message + "\n  Wingman: a review is pending and will be addressed on your next prompt."
    43→	}
    44→	return message + "\n  Wingman is active: your changes will be automatically reviewed."
    45→}
    46→
    47→// handleWingmanTurnStart checks for a pending wingman review and injects it
    48→// as additionalContext so the agent addresses it before the user's request.
    49→// Returns true if a hook response was written to stdout (caller should return early).
    50→func handleWingmanTurnStart(sessionID string) bool {
    51→	if !settings.IsWingmanEnabled() {
    52→		return false
    53→	}
    54→
    55→	repoRoot, rootErr := paths.RepoRoot()
    56→	if rootErr != nil {
    57→		return false
    58→	}
    59→
    60→	wingmanLogCtx := logging.WithComponent(context.Background(), "wingman")
    61→
    62→	// If a review is pending, check if it has actionable issues before injecting
    63→	reviewPath := filepath.Join(repoRoot, wingmanReviewFile)
    64→	if _, statErr := os.Stat(reviewPath); statErr == nil {
    65→		if !reviewHasActionableIssues(reviewPath) {
    66→			// No actionable issues — clean up and notify the user
    67→			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "[wingman] Review has no actionable issues, cleaning up\n")
    68→			logging.Info(wingmanLogCtx, "wingman review has no actionable issues, skipping injection",
    69→				slog.String("session_id", sessionID),
    70→			)
    71→			_ = os.Remove(reviewPath)
    72→			_ = outputHookMessage("[Wingman] Reviewed your changes — no issues found.") //nolint:errcheck // best-effort notification
    73→		} else {
    74→			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "[wingman] Review available: .entire/REVIEW.md — injecting into context\n")
    75→			logging.Info(wingmanLogCtx, "wingman injecting review instruction on prompt-submit",
    76→				slog.String("session_id", sessionID),
    77→			)
    78→			if err := outputHookResponseWithContextAndMessage(
    79→				wingmanApplyInstruction,
    80→				"[Wingman] A code review is pending and will be addressed before your request.",
    81→			); err != nil {
    82→				fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "[wingman] Warning: failed to inject review instruction: %v\n", err)
    83→			} else {
    84→				return true // Hook response written to stdout — caller must return
    85→			}
    86→		}
    87→	}
    88→
    89→	// Notify if a review is currently in progress (fresh lock file).
    90→	lockPath := filepath.Join(repoRoot, wingmanLockFile)
    91→	if lockInfo, statErr := os.Stat(lockPath); statErr == nil && time.Since(lockInfo.ModTime()) <= wingmanNotificationLockThreshold {
    92→		logging.Info(wingmanLogCtx, "wingman review in progress",
    93→			slog.String("session_id", sessionID),
    94→		)
    95→		if err := outputHookMessage("[Wingman] Review in progress..."); err != nil {
    96→			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "[wingman] Warning: failed to output review-in-progress message: %v\n", err)
    97→		}
    98→	}
    99→
   100→	return false
   101→}
   102→
   103→// handleWingmanTurnEnd handles wingman actions at turn end: triggering reviews,
   104→// auto-applying pending reviews, and showing stop notifications.
   105→func handleWingmanTurnEnd(sessionID string, totalChanges int, relModifiedFiles, relNewFiles, relDeletedFiles, allPrompts []string, commitMessage string) {
   106→	repoRoot, err := paths.RepoRoot()
   107→	if err != nil {
   108→		return
   109→	}
   110→
   111→	strat := GetStrategy()
   112→
   113→	// Trigger wingman review for auto-commit strategy (commit already happened
   114→	// in SaveStep). Manual-commit triggers wingman from the git post-commit hook
   115→	// instead, since the user commits manually.
   116→	if totalChanges > 0 && strat.Name() == strategy.StrategyNameAutoCommit && settings.IsWingmanEnabled() {
   117→		triggerWingmanReview(WingmanPayload{
   118→			SessionID:     sessionID,
   119→			RepoRoot:      repoRoot,
   120→			ModifiedFiles: relModifiedFiles,
   121→			NewFiles:      relNewFiles,
   122→			DeletedFiles:  relDeletedFiles,
   123→			Prompts:       allPrompts,
   124→			CommitMessage: commitMessage,
   125→		})
   126→	}
   127→
   128→	// Auto-apply pending wingman review on turn end
   129→	triggerWingmanAutoApplyIfPending(repoRoot)
   130→
   131→	outputWingmanStopNotification(repoRoot)
   132→}
   133→
   134→// triggerWingmanAutoApplyIfPending checks for a pending REVIEW.md and spawns
   135→// the auto-apply subprocess if conditions are met. Called from the stop hook
   136→// on every turn end (both with-changes and no-changes paths).
   137→//
   138→// When a live session exists, this is a no-op: the prompt-submit injection
   139→// will deliver the review visibly in the user's terminal instead. Background
   140→// auto-apply is only used when no sessions are alive (all ended).
   141→func triggerWingmanAutoApplyIfPending(repoRoot string) {
   142→	logCtx := logging.WithComponent(context.Background(), "wingman")
   143→	if !settings.IsWingmanEnabled() {
   144→		logging.Debug(logCtx, "wingman auto-apply skip: wingman not enabled")
   145→		return
   146→	}
   147→	if os.Getenv("ENTIRE_WINGMAN_APPLY") != "" {
   148→		logging.Debug(logCtx, "wingman auto-apply skip: already in apply subprocess")
   149→		return
   150→	}
   151→	reviewPath := filepath.Join(repoRoot, wingmanReviewFile)
   152→	if _, statErr := os.Stat(reviewPath); statErr != nil {
   153→		logging.Debug(logCtx, "wingman auto-apply skip: no REVIEW.md pending")
   154→		return
   155→	}
   156→	// Skip auto-apply if the review has no actionable issues
   157→	if !reviewHasActionableIssues(reviewPath) {
   158→		logging.Info(logCtx, "wingman auto-apply skip: review has no actionable issues, cleaning up")
   159→		_ = os.Remove(reviewPath)
   160→		return
   161→	}
   162→	wingmanState := loadWingmanStateDirect(repoRoot)
   163→	if wingmanState != nil && wingmanState.ApplyAttemptedAt != nil {
   164→		logging.Debug(logCtx, "wingman auto-apply already attempted, skipping",
   165→			slog.Time("attempted_at", *wingmanState.ApplyAttemptedAt),
   166→		)
   167→		return
   168→	}
   169→	// Don't spawn background auto-apply if a live session exists.
   170→	// The prompt-submit hook will inject REVIEW.md as additionalContext,
   171→	// which is visible to the user in their terminal.
   172→	if hasAnyLiveSession(repoRoot) {
   173→		logging.Debug(logCtx, "wingman auto-apply deferred: live session will handle via injection")
   174→		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "[wingman] Review pending — will be injected on next prompt\n")
   175→		return
   176→	}
   177→	fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "[wingman] Pending review found, spawning auto-apply (no live sessions)\n")
   178→	logging.Info(logCtx, "wingman auto-apply spawning (no live sessions)",
   179→		slog.String("review_path", reviewPath),
   180→	)
   181→	spawnDetachedWingmanApply(repoRoot)
   182→}
   183→
   184→// reviewHasActionableIssues reads a REVIEW.md and checks if it contains
   185→// actionable issue markers ([CRITICAL], [WARNING], or [SUGGESTION]).
   186→// Returns false if the file can't be read or contains no issues.
   187→func reviewHasActionableIssues(reviewPath string) bool {
   188→	data, err := os.ReadFile(reviewPath) //nolint:gosec // path is from repo-relative constant
   189→	if err != nil {
   190→		return false
   191→	}
   192→
   193→	content := string(data)
   194→
   195→	// The review format uses "### [SEVERITY] description" for each issue.
   196→	// Check for any of the severity markers in heading context.
   197→	for _, marker := range []string{"[CRITICAL]", "[WARNING]", "[SUGGESTION]"} {
   198→		if strings.Contains(content, marker) {
   199→			return true
   200→		}
   201→	}
   202→
   203→	return false
   204→}
   205→
   206→// outputWingmanStopNotification outputs a systemMessage notification about
   207→// wingman status at the end of a stop hook. This makes wingman activity visible
   208→// in the agent terminal without injecting context into the agent's conversation.
   209→// Best-effort: status may be stale due to concurrent wingman processes.
   210→func outputWingmanStopNotification(repoRoot string) {
   211→	if !settings.IsWingmanEnabled() {
   212→		return
   213→	}
   214→	if os.Getenv("ENTIRE_WINGMAN_APPLY") != "" {
   215→		return
   216→	}
   217→
   218→	lockPath := filepath.Join(repoRoot, wingmanLockFile)
   219→	if info, err := os.Stat(lockPath); err == nil && time.Since(info.ModTime()) <= wingmanNotificationLockThreshold {
   220→		_ = outputHookMessage("[Wingman] Reviewing your changes...") //nolint:errcheck // best-effort notification
   221→		return
   222→	}
   223→
   224→	reviewPath := filepath.Join(repoRoot, wingmanReviewFile)
   225→	if _, err := os.Stat(reviewPath); err == nil && reviewHasActionableIssues(reviewPath) {
   226→		_ = outputHookMessage("[Wingman] Review pending \u2014 will be addressed on your next prompt") //nolint:errcheck // best-effort notification
   227→		return
   228→	}
   229→}
